# ELDT Training (eldttraining.us)

> ELDT Training is an online provider of FMCSA-compliant Entry-Level Driver Training (ELDT) theory courses for commercial driver's license (CDL) applicants in all 50 US states, DC, and Puerto Rico. Courses cover Class A, Class B, the Class B to A upgrade, and the Hazmat (H), Passenger (P), School Bus (S), Tanker (N), and Hazmat + Tanker (X) endorsements. Completions are reported to the FMCSA Training Provider Registry (TPR).

Key facts:
- Federal ELDT rule: 49 CFR Part 380, Subparts F and G. Compliance date: February 7, 2022.
- ELDT applies to first-time Class A or Class B CDL applicants, Class B to Class A upgrades, and first-time H, P, or S endorsements. It does not apply to the N or T endorsements.
- Theory may be completed online with a TPR-registered provider; trainees must score at least 80% on the theory assessment. There is no federal minimum number of hours.
- Class A, Class B, P, and S also require behind-the-wheel (BTW) training with a registered BTW provider. H is theory only.
- Providers must report completions to the TPR by midnight of the second business day after the trainee finishes. State licensing agencies verify ELDT before the CDL skills test (or before the H knowledge test).
- ELDT Training courses: English only, with audio playback; self-paced; 3-month completion window and 1-year access.
- Company: ELDTtraining.us is a subsidiary of Industrial Certified Training, LLC, and partners with HAZWOPER OSHA Training, LLC. Phone (866) 429-6742. Email info@eldttraining.us.

# Full content

# Online ELDT Training (eldttraining.us)

## What is ELDT?
ELDT (Entry-Level Driver Training) is a set of federal training requirements established by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) in 49 CFR Part 380 for individuals seeking a commercial driver's license (CDL) or certain CDL endorsements for the first time. It took effect on February 7, 2022.

## Who needs to complete ELDT?
ELDT applies to individuals who are: Obtaining a Class A CDL for the first time Obtaining a Class B CDL for the first time Upgrading from a Class B to a Class A CDL Obtaining a Passenger (P) endorsement for the first time Obtaining a School Bus (S) endorsement for the first time Obtaining a Hazardous Materials (H) endorsement for the first time

## What training must an entry-level driver complete before the CDL skills or knowledge test?
To be eligible to take the Class A or Class B CDL skills test, the S or P skills test, or the H knowledge test, applicants must complete the applicable entry-level driver training from a registered training provider . Class A, Class B, P, and S require both theory and behind-the-wheel training; H requires theory only. License or endorsement ELDT verified before Theory required? Behind-the-wheel required? Class A CDL (first time or B-to-A upgrade) CDL skills test Yes Yes, range and public road Class B CDL (first time) CDL skills test Yes Yes, range and public road Passenger (P) endorsement (first time) P skills test Yes Yes, range and/or public road School bus (S) endorsement (first time) S skills test Yes Yes, range and/or public road Hazardous materials (H) endorsement (first time) H knowledge test Yes No Tank vehicle (N) endorsement Not covered by ELDT No (federal) No Doubles/triples (T) endorsement Not covered by ELDT No (federal) No Source: 49 CFR Part 380, Subparts F and G, and the FMCSA Training Provider Registry. ELDT applies to applicants who did not already hold the license or endorsement before February 7, 2022.

## When did the ELDT requirements take effect?
The federal ELDT requirements took effect on February 7, 2022. They are not retroactive: drivers who already held the applicable CDL or endorsement before that date do not need ELDT for it.

## Can I complete ELDT training online?
Yes, for the theory portion. Theory may be completed online with any provider listed on the FMCSA Training Provider Registry (TPR). For Class A, Class B, P, and S, behind-the-wheel training must still be completed in a vehicle with a qualified, TPR-registered instructor.

## How much does online ELDT cost here?
Class A is $129.99, Class B is $119.99, the Class B to A upgrade is $99.99, Hazmat (H) is $69.99, Passenger (P) and School Bus (S) are $59.99 each, the X endorsement course is $129.99, and the Tanker (N) course is $49.99.

## How fast is my completion reported to the FMCSA?
Federal rules give providers until midnight of the second business day after you finish. We submit your completion to the Training Provider Registry as soon as you pass the final theory assessment with 80% or higher.

## Is the course available in Spanish?
Not currently. Our ELDT courses are available in English only, with audio playback that reads each lesson aloud.

# Entry Level Driver Training (ELDT) - Class A

Price: $129.99 (regular $159.99) · Duration: 15 hours · 30 lessons · 80% passing score · Verified before: Class A CDL skills test · Behind-the-wheel: Yes, range and public road, with a registered BTW provider

This is the federally required Entry-Level Driver Training (ELDT) theory course for a Class A commercial driver's license . Under 49 CFR Part 380, anyone applying for a Class A CDL for the first time must complete Class A theory training with a provider listed on the FMCSA Training Provider Registry (TPR) before the state will let them take the CDL skills test.

The course follows the five-unit Class A theory curriculum in Appendix A to Part 380: basic operation, safe operating procedures, advanced operating practices, vehicle systems and malfunctions, and non-driving activities. You need 80% or higher on the final theory assessment. When you pass, we submit your completion to the TPR so your state licensing agency can see it.

Who needs it:
- First-time Class A CDL applicants who will drive tractor-trailers or other combination vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 lbs or more towing a unit over 10,000 lbs
- CLP holders who obtained their permit on or after February 7, 2022
- Drivers starting long-haul, regional, flatbed, reefer, tanker, or livestock careers
- Company-sponsored trainees whose carrier lets them pick their own TPR-registered theory provider

Syllabus:
- Module 1: Basic Operation of a Commercial Motor Vehicle: Lesson 1: Orientation; Lesson 2: Control Systems and Dashboard; Lesson 3: Pre-Trip and Post-Trip Inspections; Lesson 4: Basic Operation; Lesson 5: Shifting or Operating Transmissions; Lesson 6: Backing and Docking; Lesson 7: Coupling and Uncoupling
- Module 2: Safe Operating Procedures: Lesson 8: Visual Search; Lesson 9: Communication; Lesson 10: Distracted Driving; Lesson 11: Speed Management; Lesson 12: Space Management; Lesson 13: Night Operation; Lesson 14: Extreme Driving Conditions
- Module 3: Advanced Operating Practices: Lesson 15: Hazard Perception; Lesson 16: Skid Control, Recovery, Jackknifing, and Other Emergencies; Lesson 17: Railroad-Highway Grade Crossings
- Module 4: Vehicle Systems and Reporting Malfunctions: Lesson 18: Identification and Diagnosis of Malfunctions; Lesson 19: Roadside Inspections; Lesson 20: Vehicle Maintenance
- Module 5: Non-Driving Activities: Lesson 21: Handling and Documenting Cargo; Lesson 22: Environmental Compliance Issues; Lesson 23: Hours of Service Requirements; Lesson 24: Fatigue and Wellness Awareness; Lesson 25: Post-Crash Procedures; Lesson 26: External Communications; Lesson 27: Whistleblower and Coercion; Lesson 28: Trip Planning; Lesson 29: Drugs and Alcohol; Lesson 30: Medical Requirements
- Practice Examination

Enroll: https://eldttraining.us/checkout?item=class-a

# Entry Level Driver Training (ELDT) - Class B

Price: $119.99 (regular $159.99) · Duration: 13 hours · 29 lessons · 80% passing score · Verified before: Class B CDL skills test · Behind-the-wheel: Yes, range and public road, with a registered BTW provider

This is the federally required ELDT theory course for a Class B commercial driver's license . Anyone applying for a Class B CDL for the first time must complete Class B theory with a provider on the FMCSA Training Provider Registry before taking the Class B skills test.

It covers the Class B theory curriculum in Appendix B to 49 CFR Part 380: basic operation, safe operating procedures, advanced operating practices, vehicle systems and malfunctions, and non-driving activities such as hours of service, cargo, and post-crash procedures. Pass the final assessment with 80% or higher and we report your completion to the TPR.

Who needs it:
- First-time Class B CDL applicants driving single vehicles with a GVWR of 26,001 lbs or more (straight trucks, dump trucks, box trucks, cement mixers, garbage trucks)
- Future city bus, transit, and motorcoach drivers (add the Passenger endorsement course)
- Future school bus drivers (add the Passenger and School Bus endorsement courses)
- Municipal, utility, and construction employees whose employer requires a Class B CDL

Syllabus:
- Module 1: Basic Operation of a Commercial Motor Vehicle: Lesson 1: Orientation; Lesson 2: Control Systems and Dashboard; Lesson 3: Pre-Trip and Post-Trip Inspections; Lesson 4: Basic Operation; Lesson 5: Shifting or Operating Transmissions; Lesson 6: Backing and Docking
- Module 2: Safe Operating Procedures: Lesson 7: Visual Search; Lesson 8: Communication; Lesson 9: Distracted Driving; Lesson 10: Speed Management; Lesson 11: Space Management; Lesson 12: Night Operation; Lesson 13: Extreme Driving Conditions
- Module 3: Advanced Operating Practices: Lesson 14: Hazard Perception; Lesson 15: Skid Control, Recovery, Jackknifing, and Other Emergencies; Lesson 16: Railroad-Highway Grade Crossings
- Module 4: Vehicle Systems and Reporting Malfunctions: Lesson 17: Identification and Diagnosis of Malfunctions; Lesson 18: Roadside Inspections; Lesson 19: Vehicle Maintenance
- Module 5: Non-Driving Activities: Lesson 20: Handling and Documenting Cargo; Lesson 21: Environmental Compliance Issues; Lesson 22: Hours of Service Requirements; Lesson 23: Fatigue and Wellness Awareness; Lesson 24: Post-Crash Procedures; Lesson 25: External Communications; Lesson 26: Whistleblower and Coercion; Lesson 27: Trip Planning; Lesson 28: Drugs and Alcohol; Lesson 29: Medical Requirements
- Practice Examination

Enroll: https://eldttraining.us/checkout?item=class-b

# Entry Level Driver Training (ELDT) - Class B to A Upgrade

Price: $99.99 (regular $129.99) · Duration: 12 hours · 22 lessons · 80% passing score · Verified before: Class A CDL skills test · Behind-the-wheel: Yes, range and public road, with a registered BTW provider

Already have a Class B CDL? Under the federal ELDT rule, upgrading from Class B to Class A counts as entry-level training , so you need Class A theory and behind-the-wheel training from TPR-registered providers before the Class A skills test.

This upgrade course is built for working Class B drivers. It focuses on what changes when you move to combination vehicles (coupling and uncoupling, combination-vehicle handling, backing, and the related safety and regulatory topics) while still covering the non-driving activities in the Class A curriculum. Pass the final assessment with 80% or higher and we report your completion to the TPR.

Who needs it:
- Current Class B CDL holders upgrading to Class A
- Dump-truck, box-truck, and bus drivers moving into tractor-trailer work
- Class B drivers whose employer is adding combination vehicles to the fleet

Syllabus:
- Module 1: Basic Operation of a Commercial Motor Vehicle: Lesson 1: Orientation; Lesson 2: Control Systems and Dashboard; Lesson 3: Pre-Trip and Post-Trip Inspections; Lesson 4: Basic Operation; Lesson 5: Shifting or Operating Transmissions; Lesson 6: Backing and Docking; Lesson 7: Coupling and Uncoupling
- Module 2: Safe Operating Procedures: Lesson 8: Visual Search; Lesson 9: Communication; Lesson 10: Distracted Driving; Lesson 11: Speed Management; Lesson 12: Space Management; Lesson 13: Night Operation; Lesson 14: Extreme Driving Conditions
- Module 3: Advanced Operating Practices: Lesson 15: Hazard Perception; Lesson 16: Skid Control, Recovery, Jackknifing, and Other Emergencies; Lesson 17: Railroad-Highway Grade Crossings
- Module 4: Vehicle Systems and Reporting Malfunctions: Lesson 18: Identification and Diagnosis of Malfunctions; Lesson 19: Roadside Inspections; Lesson 20: Vehicle Maintenance
- Module 5: Non-Driving Activities: Lesson 21: Hours of Service Requirements; Lesson 22: Fatigue and Wellness Awareness
- Practice Examination

Enroll: https://eldttraining.us/checkout?item=b-to-a-upgrade

# CDL Entry Level Driver Training (ELDT) - HAZMAT (H) Endorsement

Price: $69.99 (regular $99.99) · Duration: 5 hours · 13 lessons · 80% passing score · Verified before: H endorsement knowledge test · Behind-the-wheel: No, the H endorsement is theory only

Before you can take the hazardous materials (H) endorsement knowledge test for the first time, federal rules require you to complete hazmat ELDT theory training with a provider on the FMCSA Training Provider Registry. Hazmat is the only ELDT endorsement with no behind-the-wheel component, so this online course is the entire training requirement.

The course follows the hazmat curriculum in Appendix E to 49 CFR Part 380: hazmat basics and communication (the hazmat table, shipping papers, marking, labeling, placarding), safe transportation practices, emergency response, pre-trip and operational rules, and route planning and permits. Score 80% or higher on the final assessment and we report your completion to the TPR.

Who needs it:
- CDL holders or applicants adding the H endorsement for the first time
- Drivers who plan to haul placarded loads (fuel, chemicals, gases, explosives, radioactive materials)
- Drivers working toward the X endorsement (hazmat + tank), since X requires passing the H knowledge test

Syllabus:
- Module 1: Hazmat Basic Requirements and Communication: Lesson 1: Basic Introductory Hazardous Materials Requirements; Lesson 2: Operational Hazardous Materials Requirements; Lesson 3: Reporting Hazardous Materials Crashes and Releases
- Module 2: Safe Transportation Practices: Lesson 4: Tunnels and Railroad (RR)-Highway Grade Crossing Requirements; Lesson 5: Loading and Unloading Hazardous Materials; Lesson 6: Hazardous Materials on Passenger Vehicles; Lesson 7: Bulk Packages
- Module 3: Emergency Preparedness and Response: Lesson 8: Operating Emergency Equipment; Lesson 9: Emergency Response Procedures
- Module 4: Pre-Trip and Operational Considerations: Lesson 10: Engine (Fueling); Lesson 11: Tire Check
- Module 5: Planning and Permits: Lesson 12: Routes and Route Planning; Lesson 13: Hazardous Materials Safety Permits (HMSP)
- Practice Examination

Enroll: https://eldttraining.us/checkout?item=hazmat-h

# CDL Entry Level Driver Training (ELDT) - Passenger (P) Endorsement

Price: $59.99 (regular $99.99) · Duration: 6 hours · 18 lessons · 80% passing score · Verified before: P endorsement skills test · Behind-the-wheel: Yes, range and/or public road, with a registered provider

A Passenger (P) endorsement lets you drive a commercial vehicle designed to carry 16 or more people, including the driver. If you are getting the P endorsement for the first time, the federal ELDT rule requires P endorsement theory training from a TPR-registered provider, plus behind-the-wheel training, before your P skills test.

This course covers the passenger curriculum in Appendix C to 49 CFR Part 380: vehicle orientation and inspections, post-crash and emergency procedures, passenger management and baggage, hours of service and seat-belt rules, navigating railroad crossings and highways, and security and roadside inspections. Pass the final assessment with 80% or higher and we report your completion to the TPR.

Who needs it:
- Transit, city bus, and motorcoach drivers
- Shuttle and tour drivers operating vehicles designed for 16+ occupants
- School bus drivers (who also need the School Bus endorsement)
- Church, camp, and nonprofit drivers of large passenger vans and buses

Syllabus:
- Module 1: Pre-Trip and Operational Considerations: Lesson 1: Vehicle Orientation; Lesson 2: Pre-Trip, En Route, and Post-Trip Inspection; Lesson 3: Fueling; Lesson 4: Idling
- Module 2: Emergency and Safety Procedures: Lesson 5: Post-Crash Procedures; Lesson 6: Other Emergency Procedures
- Module 3: Cargo and Passenger Management: Lesson 7: Baggage and/or Cargo Management; Lesson 8: Passenger Safety Awareness Briefing; Lesson 9: Passenger Management; Lesson 10: Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) Compliance
- Module 4: Hours of Service and Safety Regulations: Lesson 11: Hours of Service (HOS) Requirements; Lesson 12: Belt Safety; Lesson 13: Distracted Driving
- Module 5: Navigational Safety: Lesson 14: Railroad-Highway Grade Crossings and Drawbridges; Lesson 15: Weigh Stations
- Module 6: Security and Inspections: Lesson 16: Security and Crime; Lesson 17: Roadside Inspections; Lesson 18: Penalties and Fines
- Practice Examination

Enroll: https://eldttraining.us/checkout?item=passenger-p

# CDL Entry Level Driver Training (ELDT) - School Bus (S) Endorsement

Price: $59.99 (regular $99.00) · Duration: 5 hours · 11 lessons · 80% passing score · Verified before: S endorsement skills test · Behind-the-wheel: Yes, range and/or public road, with a registered provider

To drive a school bus you need a CDL with both the Passenger (P) and School Bus (S) endorsements . If you are getting the S endorsement for the first time, the federal ELDT rule requires S endorsement theory training from a TPR-registered provider and behind-the-wheel training before your S skills test.

This course follows the school bus curriculum in Appendix D to 49 CFR Part 380: danger zones and mirror use, loading and unloading, student management, railroad-highway grade crossings, emergency exit and evacuation, and special safety considerations. Pass the final assessment with 80% or higher and we report your completion to the TPR.

Who needs it:
- New school bus drivers hired by districts or contractors
- Current CDL holders adding the S endorsement
- Activity-bus and special-needs transport drivers who carry students

# CDL Entry Level Driver Training (ELDT) - Hazmat and Tank Vehicle (X) Endorsement

Price: $129.99 (regular $169.00) · Duration: 5 hours · 14 lessons · 80% passing score · Verified before: H endorsement knowledge test (the hazmat portion of X) · Behind-the-wheel: No

The X endorsement combines hazardous materials (H) and tank vehicle (N) on one CDL. To get it you pass both the hazmat and tanker knowledge tests and clear the TSA security threat assessment. Because the hazmat test is involved, first-time hazmat applicants must complete hazmat ELDT theory before testing.

This course packages the hazmat ELDT curriculum (hazmat basics and communication, safe transportation practices, emergency response, operational rules, routes and HMSP permits) with tank vehicle operation and inspection, including liquid surge, baffles and bulkheads, and cargo tank rules. 14 lessons in 5 modules, with an 80% passing score. We report your hazmat completion to the TPR.

- Drivers adding H and N at the same time
- Carriers training new tanker drivers who will haul placarded bulk loads

- Final Examination

# CDL Entry Level Driver Training (ELDT) - Tanker (N) Endorsement

Price: $49.99 (regular $99.99) · Duration: 1 hours · 2 lessons · 80% passing score · Verified before: N endorsement knowledge test (state) · Behind-the-wheel: No

The tank vehicle (N) endorsement is required to drive a CMV that carries liquids or gases in tanks with an individual capacity over 119 gallons and an aggregate capacity of 1,000 gallons or more. To get it, you pass your state's tanker knowledge test.

Good to know: the federal ELDT rule covers Class A, Class B, and the H, P, and S endorsements. It does not require ELDT for the N endorsement. This course is tank vehicle training that prepares you for the N knowledge test and gives employers documented training: regulations and endorsement rules, tank design (bulkheads, baffles, smooth-bore tanks), liquid surge and rollover risk, valves, manhole covers and emergency shutoffs, and safe driving with partial loads. Hauling hazmat in a tank? Choose the X endorsement course instead.

Who needs it:
- CDL holders adding the N endorsement
- Drivers starting milk, water, food-grade liquid, or non-hazmat chemical tanker jobs
- Employers that want documented tank vehicle training for new drivers

Syllabus:
- Lesson 1: Regulatory Overview
- Lesson 2: Tank Vehicles Operation and Inspection
- Final Examination

Enroll: https://eldttraining.us/checkout?item=tanker-n

# How to Choose the Best Online ELDT Training Provider

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/best-online-eldt-training
Updated: 2026-11-16

**The best online ELDT provider for you is one that is active on the FMCSA Training Provider Registry for your training type, reports completions quickly, is priced transparently, and fits how you learn** (mobile, audio, self-paced). Registration is non-negotiable: training from a provider that isn't listed, or that was removed, doesn't count. After that, compare price, course length, support, and refund policy.

## The 8-point checklist

1. **Active on the TPR for your training type.** Search the [Training Provider Registry](/guides/training-provider-registry) and confirm the provider offers theory for Class A, Class B, P, S, or H, whichever you need.
2. **Clear, all-in price.** The price should include the final assessment and TPR reporting. Watch for add-on "filing fees."
3. **Fast reporting.** The legal deadline is midnight of the second business day. Better providers report as soon as you pass.
4. **Full curriculum.** The course should cover every unit in the federal curriculum, with a final assessment requiring 80% or higher.
5. **Fits your learning style.** Mobile-friendly design, audio narration, progress saving, and practice quizzes make a real difference.
6. **Reasonable completion window.** Look for enough time to finish and review before your tests.
7. **Real support.** A phone number, email, and posted hours, so you can get help with login or reporting questions.
8. **Fair refund policy.** Know what happens if you change your plans.

## How ELDT Training compares on the checklist

| Checklist item | ELDT Training |
|---|---|
| Registered on the TPR | Yes, ELDT theory provider |
| Price (Class A) | $129.99, TPR reporting included |
| Reporting | Submitted when you pass the final assessment |
| Course length (Class A) | About 15 hours, 30 lessons |
| Audio playback | Yes, every lesson |
| Devices | Phone, tablet, computer |
| Completion window | 3 months to finish, 1 year of access |
| Support | (866) 429-6742 and info@eldttraining.us |
| Refund policy | 30-day refund policy (conditions apply) |
| Language | English only |

## Online theory vs a full CDL school

If you're starting from zero and want everything in one place, a CDL school that offers theory and BTW can be simpler. If you want to save money, keep working while you study, or already have a BTW provider lined up (such as an employer), online theory plus separate BTW is often the better value. Both paths are equally valid under federal rules as long as each provider is registered.

## Questions to ask any provider

- Which training types are you registered for on the TPR?
- When exactly do you submit my completion?
- What happens if I fail the final assessment?
- Can I access the course on my phone, and does it have audio?
- How long do I have to finish?
- What's your refund policy?

## Frequently asked questions

### Is the cheapest ELDT course good enough?
Any course from an active registered provider satisfies the federal requirement. The difference is in experience: learning quality, support, and reporting speed. Be cautious with extremely low prices from providers you can't verify on the TPR.

### Are FMCSA-approved ELDT courses better?
FMCSA doesn't approve or rank individual courses. Providers self-certify and are listed on the TPR, and FMCSA can audit and remove them. "TPR-registered" is the accurate term.

### Do employers prefer certain ELDT providers?
Most employers care that training is valid on the TPR and that you can pass your tests. Some carriers that run their own programs require you to train with them.

### Can I switch providers partway through?
Yes, but you'd generally have to complete the full theory course with the new provider, since each provider certifies its own complete training.
