# CDL Endorsements: The Complete List (H, N, P, S, T, X)

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/cdl-endorsements
Updated: 2026-11-16

**There are six CDL endorsements: H (Hazardous Materials), N (Tank Vehicle), P (Passenger), S (School Bus), T (Doubles/Triples), and X (combined Hazmat and Tank Vehicle).** Each requires a knowledge test. P and S also require a skills test. Under the federal ELDT rule, first-time H, P, and S endorsements require Entry-Level Driver Training; N and T don't. Hazmat endorsements (H and X) also require a TSA security threat assessment.

## CDL endorsements at a glance

| Code | Endorsement | Lets you drive | Tests | ELDT required? | Our course |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **H** | Hazardous Materials | Vehicles hauling placarded hazmat | Knowledge + TSA check | **Yes** (theory) | [$69.99](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-hazmat-h-endorsement) |
| **N** | Tank Vehicle | Liquid/gas tanks >119 gal each, ≥1,000 gal total | Knowledge | No (federal) | [$49.99](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-tanker-n-endorsement) |
| **P** | Passenger | Vehicles designed for 16+ occupants incl. driver | Knowledge + skills | **Yes** (theory + BTW) | [$59.99](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-passenger-p-endorsement) |
| **S** | School Bus | School buses (also requires P) | Knowledge + skills | **Yes** (theory + BTW) | [$59.99](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-school-bus-s-endorsement) |
| **T** | Doubles/Triples | Double and triple trailers (Class A) | Knowledge | No | — |
| **X** | Hazmat + Tanker | Hazmat in tank vehicles | H + N knowledge + TSA | **Yes** (hazmat theory) | [$129.99](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-hazmat-and-tank-vehicle-endorsement) |

## Hazmat (H)
Required to haul hazardous materials in amounts that require placards. You need hazmat ELDT theory, the H knowledge test, and a TSA security threat assessment with fingerprints. Usually the highest-paying single endorsement. Full guide: [hazmat endorsement](/guides/hazmat-endorsement).

## Tank Vehicle (N)
Required for tanks with an individual capacity over 119 gallons and aggregate capacity of 1,000 gallons or more. Knowledge test only; ELDT isn't federally required. Full guide: [tanker endorsement](/guides/tanker-endorsement).

## Passenger (P)
Required for vehicles designed to carry 16 or more people including the driver: transit buses, motorcoaches, shuttles. Requires P ELDT (theory and BTW), a knowledge test, and a skills test. Full guide: [passenger endorsement](/guides/passenger-endorsement).

## School Bus (S)
Required to drive a school bus, in addition to P. Requires S ELDT (theory and BTW), a knowledge test, and a skills test in a school bus. Full guide: [school bus endorsement](/guides/school-bus-endorsement).

## Doubles/Triples (T)
Required to pull double or triple trailers with a Class A. Knowledge test only. Triples are legal only on certain routes in some states. Full guide: [doubles/triples endorsement](/guides/doubles-triples-endorsement).

## X (Hazmat + Tanker)
Issued when you qualify for both H and N. Covers placarded hazmat in tanks, like gasoline. Full guide: [X endorsement](/guides/x-endorsement).

## Which endorsements should you get?

- **Most job options as a Class A driver:** H, N (or X), and T
- **Fuel and chemical hauling:** X
- **Bus and transit:** P (Class B)
- **School bus:** P + S
- **Food-grade liquids, water, milk:** N

## Frequently asked questions

### How many CDL endorsements are there?
Six: H, N, P, S, T, and X. Some states also use additional state-specific codes.

### What endorsements are required for a Class A CDL?
None are required to get a Class A. You add endorsements based on the work you'll do. Many Class A drivers add H, N, and T to qualify for more jobs.

### Which CDL endorsements require ELDT?
First-time H, P, and S endorsements. X requires hazmat ELDT if you don't already have an H endorsement. N and T don't require ELDT.

### Can I get endorsements on my CDL permit?
Only P, S, and N can appear on a CLP, with restrictions (no passengers for P/S; empty tanks only for N). Hazmat can't be added to a CLP.

### Which endorsement pays the most?
Hazmat and tanker (or X) generally open the highest-paying specialized freight jobs.

---

# English Language Proficiency Rules for CDL Drivers

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/cdl-english-language-proficiency
Updated: 2026-11-16

**Federal rules (49 CFR 391.11(b)(2)) require commercial drivers to read and speak English well enough to converse with the public, understand highway traffic signs and signals, respond to official inquiries, and make entries on reports and records.** Since June 25, 2025, inspectors have placed drivers who fail this standard at roadside out of service. FMCSA has also cited English-proficiency problems when removing training providers from the Training Provider Registry in 2026.

## What the rule requires

A driver must be able to:

- Read and speak English sufficiently to converse with the general public
- Understand highway traffic signs and signals in English
- Respond to official inquiries (for example, from law enforcement or inspectors)
- Make entries on reports and records (logs, inspection reports, shipping papers)

## What changed in 2025

The English proficiency requirement isn't new, but for several years a violation by itself didn't take a driver off the road. Following a 2025 executive order, the out-of-service criteria were updated so that, starting **June 25, 2025**, a driver found not proficient during a roadside inspection is placed **out of service** and can't continue driving until the issue is resolved.

## How it's checked

Inspectors typically assess proficiency by talking with the driver in English during the inspection and checking whether the driver can read and explain road signs. Interpreters and translation apps aren't a substitute during this assessment.

## What this means for new drivers

- **Training:** Many ELDT courses, including ours, are delivered in English. This also helps you practice the vocabulary used on the job.
- **Testing:** States administer CDL knowledge and skills tests under their own policies, but the on-the-job standard is English.
- **Providers:** In 2026, FMCSA announced emergency removals of training providers after finding English proficiency violations among their graduates. Check that your provider is active on the [Training Provider Registry](/guides/training-provider-registry).

## How to prepare

- Learn the English terms for every pre-trip inspection item and vehicle control
- Practice explaining what road signs mean, out loud
- Practice common conversations: with dispatch, shippers, receivers, and officers
- Use audio playback in your ELDT course to hear terms pronounced

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I take the CDL test in another language?
Some states offer knowledge tests in other languages. That doesn't change the federal on-the-job requirement that drivers read and speak English sufficiently.

### Is ELDT Training available in Spanish?
No. Our courses are English only, with audio playback that reads each lesson aloud.

### What happens if I'm placed out of service for English proficiency?
You can't continue operating the CMV at that time; another qualified driver must move the vehicle. Your employer will need to address the issue before you return to driving.

### Does this apply to intrastate drivers?
Federal driver qualification rules apply to interstate drivers, and most states adopt similar rules for intrastate commerce. Check your state's requirements.

---

# CDL Jobs: What You Can Do With Each License and Endorsement

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/cdl-jobs
Updated: 2026-11-16

**A Class A CDL opens the most jobs: long-haul, regional, and local tractor-trailer work, plus tanker, flatbed, and hazmat freight with endorsements. A Class B CDL covers local jobs like dump truck, delivery, garbage, and bus driving. Class C covers smaller passenger and hazmat vehicles.** Endorsements (H, N, X, P, S, T) unlock specialized, often better-paying work, and first-time H, P, and S endorsements require ELDT.

## Jobs by license and the training you'll need

| Job | License | Endorsements | ELDT courses |
|---|---|---|---|
| Over-the-road (OTR) truck driver | Class A | Optional H, N, T | [Class A](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-a) |
| Regional/local tractor-trailer | Class A | Optional | Class A |
| Fuel tanker driver | Class A (or B) | X | Class A + [X](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-hazmat-and-tank-vehicle-endorsement) |
| Chemical / hazmat freight | Class A | H (often X) | Class A + [Hazmat](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-hazmat-h-endorsement) |
| Milk, water, food-grade tanker | Class A or B | N | Class A or B (+ optional [N](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-tanker-n-endorsement)) |
| LTL linehaul (doubles) | Class A | T | Class A |
| Flatbed / heavy haul | Class A | Optional | Class A |
| Dump truck / construction | Class B (A if towing) | — | [Class B](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-b) |
| Box truck / local delivery 26,001+ lbs | Class B | — | Class B |
| Garbage / recycling truck | Class B | — | Class B |
| City or transit bus | Class B | P | Class B + [Passenger](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-passenger-p-endorsement) |
| Motorcoach / charter | Class B | P | Class B + Passenger |
| School bus | Class B (or C) | P + S | Class B + Passenger + [School Bus](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-school-bus-s-endorsement) |
| Shuttle bus (16+ seats, under 26,001 lbs) | Class C | P | Passenger |
| Propane / small hazmat delivery | Class B or C | H (or X) | Hazmat (+ Class B if needed) |

## Class A jobs

Class A is the broadest license. Beyond OTR, many Class A jobs are local or regional with daily home time: port drayage, dedicated routes for retailers, intermodal, and private fleet delivery. Adding endorsements raises earning potential.

## Class B jobs

Class B jobs are mostly local with predictable schedules, often with municipal or union benefits: public works, utilities, waste, construction, beverage and building-supply delivery, and transit.

## Endorsements that pay off

- **Hazmat (H) / X:** fuel, chemicals, gases; typically higher pay
- **Tanker (N):** liquid bulk, food-grade, water
- **Doubles/Triples (T):** LTL linehaul
- **Passenger (P) / School Bus (S):** transit, charter, and school transportation

## Frequently asked questions

### What's the best CDL to get for jobs?
Class A, because it covers Class B vehicles too and opens the most freight jobs. Choose Class B if you're certain you want local straight-truck or bus work.

### Can I get a local job with a Class A?
Yes. Many Class A jobs are local or regional, especially drayage, dedicated, and private fleet work.

### Do I need endorsements to get hired?
Not always, but endorsements make you eligible for more jobs and often higher pay.

### Can I get a CDL job at 18?
Yes, for intrastate work in most states. Interstate jobs generally require you to be 21. See [CDL age requirements](/guides/how-old-to-get-a-cdl).

---

# CDL Permit (CLP): How to Get Your Commercial Learner's Permit

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/cdl-permit-clp
Updated: 2026-11-16

**A CDL permit, officially a commercial learner's permit (CLP), lets you drive a commercial vehicle on public roads while accompanied by a qualified CDL holder.** To get one, you need a valid driver's license, a DOT medical certificate, and passing scores on your state's CDL knowledge tests. You must hold the CLP for at least 14 days before taking the CDL skills test. A CLP is valid for up to one year (state rules vary). You don't need a CLP to start ELDT theory, but you need one for behind-the-wheel training on public roads.

## CLP requirements

- Valid non-commercial driver's license from your state of domicile
- Minimum age (18 for intrastate, 21 for interstate)
- Proof of identity, lawful presence, and residency
- DOT medical examiner's certificate
- Passing scores on the required [knowledge tests](/guides/cdl-permit-test)
- Driving record check and Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse query

## Which knowledge tests you need

| Test | Who takes it |
|---|---|
| General Knowledge | Everyone |
| Air Brakes | Anyone testing in an air-brake vehicle (most trucks) |
| Combination Vehicles | Class A applicants |
| Passenger | P endorsement |
| School Bus | S endorsement (plus Passenger) |
| Tanker | N endorsement |
| Doubles/Triples | T endorsement |
| Hazmat | H endorsement (requires hazmat ELDT first) |

## CLP rules you must follow

- **Accompanied driving only.** A CLP holder must be accompanied by a CDL holder with the proper class and endorsements, seated in the front seat (or directly behind the driver on a bus where that's how the vehicle is designed).
- **14-day minimum.** You can't take the skills test until you've held the CLP at least 14 days.
- **Limited endorsements.** Only P, S, and N endorsements can be placed on a CLP. P and S CLP holders may not carry passengers other than trainers, examiners, and other trainees. N CLP holders may only drive empty tank vehicles, and may not drive a tank that previously held hazardous materials unless it has been purged of all residue.
- **No hazmat on a CLP.** You can't haul placarded hazardous materials with a CLP.

## How long is a CLP valid?

Federal rules allow a CLP to be valid for no more than one year from issuance. Some states issue shorter permits with a renewal option. If your CLP expires before you test, you may need to retake knowledge tests. Plan your ELDT and skills test within this window.

## CLP and ELDT: what order?

FMCSA doesn't require a CLP before ELDT theory. Many people complete online theory first because it covers the same material as the knowledge tests and can start immediately. You do need a CLP before behind-the-wheel training on public roads, and you need both theory and BTW reported to the Training Provider Registry before the skills test.

## Frequently asked questions

### How long do I have to wait after getting my CLP to take the CDL test?
At least 14 days under 49 CFR 383.25. Many drivers use that time to complete behind-the-wheel training.

### Can I drive alone with a CDL permit?
No. A qualified CDL holder must accompany you whenever you drive a CMV with a CLP.

### Do I need ELDT to get my CDL permit?
No. ELDT is required before the skills test (or the H knowledge test), not before the CLP.

### Can I get my CLP online?
Some states offer online knowledge testing or appointment scheduling, but most require you to visit an office for documents, photos, and vision screening. Check your state licensing agency's website.

### What happens if my CLP expires?
You may need to renew it or retake the knowledge tests, depending on your state. Your ELDT records stay in the registry.

---

# CDL Permit Test: What's on It and How to Pass

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/cdl-permit-test
Updated: 2026-11-16

**The CDL permit test is a set of multiple-choice knowledge tests at your state licensing agency.** Everyone takes General Knowledge (typically 50 questions). Most truck drivers also take Air Brakes (about 25), Class A applicants take Combination Vehicles (about 20), and endorsement tests are added as needed. You need about **80%** to pass each test. Pass them and you get your commercial learner's permit (CLP).

## CDL knowledge tests at a glance

| Test | Typical questions | Who takes it |
|---|---|---|
| General Knowledge | 50 | Everyone |
| Air Brakes | 25 | Anyone driving air-brake vehicles |
| Combination Vehicles | 20 | Class A |
| Passenger | 20 | P endorsement |
| School Bus | 20 | S endorsement |
| Tanker | 20 | N endorsement |
| Doubles/Triples | 20 | T endorsement |
| Hazardous Materials | 30 | H endorsement (requires hazmat ELDT first) |

Question counts follow the common national format; your state may differ slightly. The passing score is typically 80% per test.

## What the General Knowledge test covers

- Vehicle inspection and the pre-trip routine
- Basic vehicle control: shifting, backing, steering
- Seeing, communicating, space and speed management
- Night driving, fog, winter, hot weather, mountain driving
- Railroad crossings and emergencies (skids, brake failure, fires)
- Hours of service and staying alert
- Alcohol, drugs, and illness
- Hazardous materials basics
- Cargo securement

## Study tips that work

1. **Read your state's CDL manual** sections for every test you'll take. Questions come from it.
2. **Take practice tests** until you consistently score 90%+.
3. **Learn the numbers:** following distances, air pressure ranges, stopping distances, placard thresholds.
4. **Do ELDT theory first.** Online theory covers the same knowledge areas in more depth and can start before your permit.
5. **Don't skip Air Brakes.** It's the test most people fail, and failing it puts an L restriction on your license.

## After you pass

You'll get your CLP. Hold it at least 14 days before the skills test, complete ELDT theory and BTW, and practice the [pre-trip inspection](/guides/pre-trip-inspection-checklist).

## Frequently asked questions

### How many questions are on the CDL permit test?
General Knowledge typically has 50 questions. Your total depends on which other tests you take: Air Brakes (about 25), Combination (about 20), and any endorsements.

### What score do you need to pass the CDL permit test?
Typically 80% on each test, for example 40 of 50 on General Knowledge.

### Can I take the CDL permit test online?
Some states offer online or remote knowledge testing; most require an in-person test. Check your state agency.

### Is the ELDT test the same as the permit test?
No. The ELDT theory assessment is given by your training provider and reported to the FMCSA registry. The permit tests are state knowledge tests. See [ELDT test](/guides/eldt-test).

---

# CDL Requirements: Everything You Need to Qualify

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/cdl-requirements
Updated: 2026-11-16

**To get a CDL you must be at least 18 (21 for interstate driving or hazmat), hold a valid driver's license from your state of domicile, prove identity and lawful presence, pass a DOT physical, read and speak English sufficiently, not be prohibited in the FMCSA Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse, pass CDL knowledge tests for a learner's permit, complete ELDT for a first-time Class A or B, and pass the skills test.** Your state may add requirements such as residency documents or a clean driving-record period.

## Federal CDL requirements checklist

| Requirement | Details |
|---|---|
| Age | 18+ for intrastate; 21+ for interstate commerce (49 CFR 391.11) |
| Driver's license | Valid non-commercial license from your state of domicile |
| Identity and lawful presence | Documents proving U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residence (rules for non-domiciled applicants are stricter) |
| Medical certification | DOT physical by a National Registry examiner, certificate valid up to 24 months |
| English proficiency | Read and speak English well enough to converse, understand signs, respond to officials, and complete reports |
| Clearinghouse | Not in "prohibited" status in the FMCSA Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse |
| Driving record | 10-year record check across all states; disqualifications must be resolved |
| Knowledge tests | General Knowledge plus class- and endorsement-specific tests for your CLP |
| CLP holding period | At least 14 days before the skills test |
| ELDT | Required for first-time Class A, Class B, B-to-A upgrade, and first-time H, P, S |
| Skills test | Vehicle inspection, basic control, and road test in a representative vehicle |

## Age requirements

You can get a CDL at 18 in most states, but it will be restricted to **intrastate** driving (within your state) until you turn 21. Interstate commerce, and in practice hazmat, require you to be 21. See [how old you have to be to get a CDL](/guides/how-old-to-get-a-cdl).

## Medical requirements

You'll need a DOT physical covering vision (at least 20/40 in each eye, with or without correction), hearing, blood pressure, and overall health, plus a urinalysis screen. Certain conditions (insulin-treated diabetes, vision in one eye, seizures) have specific rules or exemption programs. See [DOT physical and medical card](/guides/dot-physical-medical-card).

## English language proficiency

Federal rules (49 CFR 391.11(b)(2)) require commercial drivers to read and speak English sufficiently. Since June 25, 2025, inspectors have placed drivers out of service for English proficiency violations at roadside. See [CDL English language proficiency](/guides/cdl-english-language-proficiency).

## Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse

Since November 18, 2024, state licensing agencies must check the FMCSA Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse before issuing, renewing, upgrading, or transferring a CLP or CDL. A driver in "prohibited" status can't get or keep CDL privileges until completing the return-to-duty process.

## Class A vs Class B requirements

The personal requirements are the same. The differences are the tests and training:

- **Class A:** Combination Vehicles knowledge test, [Class A ELDT](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-a), and a skills test in a combination vehicle.
- **Class B:** [Class B ELDT](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-b) and a skills test in a single heavy vehicle.
- **Air brakes:** test in a vehicle with air brakes and pass the Air Brakes knowledge test, or your CDL will carry an air brake restriction.

## Endorsement requirements

- **Hazmat (H):** H knowledge test, [hazmat ELDT](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-hazmat-h-endorsement), TSA security threat assessment. See [hazmat endorsement](/guides/hazmat-endorsement).
- **Passenger (P) and School Bus (S):** knowledge test, ELDT, and skills test in a representative vehicle.
- **Tanker (N) and Doubles/Triples (T):** knowledge tests only.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need a high school diploma to get a CDL?
No federal education requirement exists. Some employers and schools set their own.

### Can I get a CDL with a DUI?
It depends on timing and your state. A DUI in a CMV, or certain offenses while holding a CDL, leads to disqualification periods. Older DUIs may affect employment more than eligibility. Check with your state licensing agency.

### Do I need a CDL to drive a box truck?
Only if the truck's GVWR is 26,001 lbs or more (Class B), it tows a heavy trailer (Class A), it carries 16+ passengers, or it hauls placarded hazmat. Many rental box trucks are under 26,001 lbs.

### Can non-citizens get a CDL?
Lawful permanent residents can apply like citizens. Rules for non-domiciled CDLs issued to certain foreign nationals have tightened and been subject to recent federal rulemaking and litigation, so check your state's current requirements.

---

# CDL Restrictions Explained: What L, Z, E, O, M, N, K, and V Mean

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/cdl-restrictions
Updated: 2026-11-16

**CDL restrictions are codes that limit which vehicles you can drive.** The most common are L (no air brakes), Z (no full air brakes), E (no manual transmission), O (no tractor-trailer), M and N (passenger vehicle class limits), K (intrastate only), and V (medical variance). Most restrictions come from the vehicle you use on the skills test. Removing L, Z, or E restrictions doesn't require ELDT; you typically just test in the right vehicle.

## Common CDL restriction codes

| Code | Meaning | How you get it |
|---|---|---|
| **L** | No air brake equipped CMV | Failing or skipping the Air Brakes knowledge test, or testing in a vehicle without air brakes |
| **Z** | No full air brake equipped CMV | Testing in a vehicle with air-over-hydraulic brakes |
| **E** | No manual transmission CMV | Taking the skills test in an automatic |
| **O** | No tractor-trailer CMV | Class A test in a combination without a fifth-wheel connection (e.g., truck and pintle-hook trailer) |
| **M** | No Class A passenger vehicle | Class A holder with P/S endorsement tested in a Class B passenger vehicle |
| **N** | No Class A or B passenger vehicle | Class B holder with P/S endorsement tested in a Class C passenger vehicle |
| **K** | Intrastate only | Under 21, or doesn't meet interstate medical requirements |
| **V** | Medical variance | Driving under an FMCSA medical exemption or skill performance evaluation |
| **P** | No passengers in CMV bus | CLP holders with a P endorsement |
| **X** | No cargo in CMV tank vehicle | CLP holders with an N endorsement |

Note: the **N restriction** (passenger vehicle limit) is different from the **N endorsement** (tank vehicles).

## How to avoid restrictions

- Pass the **Air Brakes** knowledge test and test in a vehicle with full air brakes to avoid L and Z.
- Test in a **manual transmission** if you might drive one; many carriers now run automatics, so E may not matter for your job.
- For Class A, test in a **tractor-trailer** to avoid O.

## How to remove a restriction

Removing L, Z, or E typically means passing the relevant knowledge test (for L) and/or a skills test in a vehicle with the right equipment. The federal ELDT rule doesn't apply to removing these restrictions. K comes off when you turn 21 and meet interstate requirements, usually through a visit to your state agency.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does an automatic transmission restriction matter?
It depends on your job. Many fleets now run automated manual transmissions, but some jobs (construction, older equipment) still require a manual. An E restriction rules those out.

### Do I need ELDT to remove the air brake restriction?
No. Removing L or Z restrictions isn't covered by ELDT. Check your state's process; it usually involves the Air Brakes knowledge test and a skills test in an air-brake vehicle.

### What's the difference between a restriction and an endorsement?
Endorsements add privileges (hazmat, tanker, passenger). Restrictions take privileges away. See [CDL endorsements](/guides/cdl-endorsements).

### Can I get a Class A without air brakes?
Yes, with an L restriction, but nearly all tractor-trailers have air brakes, so it severely limits your options.

---

# The CDL Skills Test: Pre-Trip, Backing, and Road Test Explained

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/cdl-skills-test
Updated: 2026-11-16

**The CDL skills test has three parts: (1) a vehicle inspection (pre-trip), (2) basic vehicle control (backing maneuvers), and (3) an on-road driving test**, all in a vehicle representative of the license class you want. You can take it after holding your CLP for at least 14 days and only once your state confirms your ELDT theory and behind-the-wheel records in the FMCSA Training Provider Registry. Failing any part usually ends the test for that day.

## Before the test: ELDT verification

For a first-time Class A or Class B CDL, a B-to-A upgrade, or a first-time P or S endorsement, the state must verify both ELDT theory and BTW records before administering the skills test. Make sure both providers have reported. See [ELDT certificate](/guides/eldt-certificate).

## Part 1: Vehicle inspection

You'll walk the examiner through inspecting the vehicle, naming each component and explaining what you're checking for. It typically includes:

- Engine compartment (fluids, belts, hoses, leaks)
- Cab check and engine start (gauges, warning lights, controls, emergency equipment)
- In-cab air brake check (for air-brake vehicles)
- External inspection: lights, steering, suspension, brakes, wheels and tires
- Coupling system and trailer (Class A)
- Bus-specific items (passenger and school bus tests)

Use our [pre-trip inspection checklist](/guides/pre-trip-inspection-checklist) to practice.

## Part 2: Basic vehicle control

The examiner selects maneuvers from:

- Straight-line backing
- Offset backing (left or right)
- Parallel parking (sight side or conventional/blind side)
- Alley dock (90-degree backing)

You're scored on encroachments (touching or crossing boundaries), pull-ups (stopping and pulling forward to reposition), and final position. Getting out to look (GOAL) is allowed a limited number of times.

## Part 3: Road test

You'll drive a set route covering turns, intersections, lane changes, highway merges, curves, railroad crossings, and possibly an upgrade/downgrade and a simulated stop. Examiners watch for:

- Mirror checks and visual search
- Proper signaling and lane position
- Speed and following distance
- Smooth shifting and braking
- Safe turns without curb strikes
- Full stops and correct railroad crossing procedure

## Common reasons people fail

- Forgetting steps of the in-cab air brake check
- Too many pull-ups or encroachments in backing
- Rolling stops, missed mirror checks, or curb strikes on turns
- Not wearing a seat belt, or other serious safety errors (automatic fail)

## Your test vehicle determines restrictions

Testing in an automatic transmission adds an E restriction; testing without air brakes adds L or Z; a Class A test in a combination without a fifth wheel adds O. See [CDL restrictions](/guides/cdl-restrictions).

## Frequently asked questions

### How long is the CDL skills test?
Usually 1.5 to 3 hours for all three parts, depending on the state and vehicle.

### Can I take the skills test in another state?
Many states let you test where you trained and transfer results to your home state. Ask both states first.

### What happens if I fail one part?
Typically the test stops, and you retest that part (or the whole test) later under your state's rules and fees. Your ELDT records stay valid in the registry.

### Do I need my own truck for the skills test?
You need a representative vehicle that passes safety checks. BTW providers often supply one for testing.

---

# Class A CDL: What It Is, What You Can Drive, and How to Get One

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/class-a-cdl
Updated: 2026-11-16

**A Class A CDL lets you drive any combination of vehicles with a gross combination weight rating (GCWR) of 26,001 lbs or more, where the towed unit weighs more than 10,000 lbs** (49 CFR 383.91). That covers tractor-trailers, truck-and-trailer combinations, tankers, flatbeds, and livestock haulers. With the right endorsements, a Class A also covers most Class B and C vehicles. First-time Class A applicants must complete Class A ELDT theory and behind-the-wheel training before the skills test.

## What can you drive with a Class A CDL?

- Tractor-trailers (semis, 18-wheelers)
- Truck and trailer combinations (for example, a dump truck pulling a heavy equipment trailer)
- Tanker trucks (with N or X endorsement)
- Flatbeds and car haulers
- Livestock trailers
- Doubles and triples (with T endorsement)
- Most Class B and C vehicles, with any required endorsements (P for buses, for example)

## Class A CDL requirements

- Age 18 (intrastate) or 21 (interstate)
- DOT medical certificate
- CLP with General Knowledge, Air Brakes, and **Combination Vehicles** tests passed
- 14-day CLP holding period
- **[Class A ELDT](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-a)** theory (80%+) and BTW from registered providers
- Skills test in a representative combination vehicle

## What Class A ELDT covers

Class A theory follows Appendix A to 49 CFR Part 380 across five units: basic operation (including coupling and uncoupling), safe operating procedures, advanced operating practices, vehicle systems and malfunctions, and non-driving activities like hours of service and trip planning. Our Class A course packages this into 30 lessons (about 15 hours). BTW adds range skills (backing maneuvers, coupling) and public-road driving.

## How to get a Class A CDL

1. Get a DOT physical.
2. Pass the Class A knowledge tests for your CLP.
3. Start [Class A ELDT theory online](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-a).
4. Hold your CLP 14 days while completing theory.
5. Complete Class A BTW with a registered provider.
6. Pass the skills test: pre-trip inspection, basic control, road test.

Already have a Class B? Take the [Class B to A upgrade](/guides/class-b-to-class-a-upgrade) path instead.

## Class A CDL jobs

Long-haul (OTR), regional, and local freight; dedicated routes; flatbed; reefer; tanker; hazmat; intermodal and port drayage; car hauling; and owner-operator work. See [CDL jobs by license](/guides/cdl-jobs).

## Frequently asked questions

### Can a Class A CDL drive a Class B truck?
Yes. A Class A license lets you drive Class B and C vehicles too, as long as you hold any endorsements the vehicle requires (for example, P for a bus) and have no restriction that prevents it.

### How long does it take to get a Class A CDL?
Typically 4 to 8 weeks, with a 14-day minimum CLP period. Full-time Class A schools often run 3 to 7 weeks.

### How much does a Class A CDL cost?
Roughly $3,000 to $10,000 at private schools, much less with online ELDT theory plus separate BTW, or employer-paid training. Our Class A theory course is $129.99.

### What's the hardest part of getting a Class A?
Most people say the air brakes portion of the pre-trip inspection and the backing maneuvers. Theory training and lots of range practice help.

---

# Class A vs Class B CDL: Which One Should You Get?

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/class-a-vs-class-b-cdl
Updated: 2026-11-16

**The difference is towing: a Class A CDL covers combination vehicles over 26,000 lbs towing more than 10,000 lbs (tractor-trailers), while a Class B CDL covers heavy single vehicles 26,001+ lbs that tow 10,000 lbs or less (dump trucks, box trucks, buses).** Class A covers Class B vehicles too, opens more jobs, and usually pays more, but takes a bit more training. If you're unsure, Class A is the more flexible choice, and completing Class A ELDT also lets you take the Class B skills test.

## Class A vs Class B at a glance

| | Class A | Class B |
|---|---|---|
| Vehicle type | Combination vehicles | Single heavy vehicles |
| Weight rule | GCWR 26,001+ lbs, towed unit >10,000 lbs | GVWR 26,001+ lbs, towing ≤10,000 lbs |
| Examples | Tractor-trailers, tankers, flatbeds | Dump trucks, box trucks, buses, garbage trucks |
| Can drive the other class? | Yes, can drive Class B and C | No Class A vehicles |
| Extra knowledge test | Combination Vehicles | None |
| ELDT course | [Class A](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-a) ($129.99, ~15 hrs) | [Class B](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-b) ($119.99, ~13 hrs) |
| BTW range skills | Includes coupling/uncoupling | No coupling |
| Typical job style | OTR, regional, local | Mostly local, home daily |

## Which should you get?

**Choose Class A if** you want the most job options, over-the-road or regional trucking, tanker or flatbed work, or the highest earning potential.

**Choose Class B if** you know you want a local job driving a dump truck, delivery truck, garbage truck, or bus, and you don't plan to tow heavy trailers.

Upgrading from Class B to Class A later counts as entry-level training under federal rules, so you'd complete Class A ELDT then. If there's a real chance you'll want Class A, it's usually cheaper to start there.

## Pay and job outlook

Class A drivers generally have access to more and higher-paying jobs, especially long-haul and specialized freight. Class B jobs often trade some pay for predictable local schedules and benefits, especially in municipal, utility, and transit work. Endorsements (hazmat, tanker, passenger) raise earning potential in both classes. See [CDL endorsements](/guides/cdl-endorsements).

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Class A harder than Class B?
A little. Class A adds the Combination Vehicles test, coupling and uncoupling, and more challenging backing with a trailer. Most people who train properly pass either.

### Can I drive a bus with a Class A CDL?
Yes, if you have the Passenger (P) endorsement (and S for school buses) and no restriction preventing it.

### Does Class A ELDT cover Class B?
Yes. FMCSA allows drivers who completed Class A ELDT to take the Class B skills test. Class B ELDT doesn't qualify you for Class A.

### What's a Class C CDL?
Class C covers smaller vehicles that carry 16+ passengers or placarded hazmat. See [ELDT for Class C](/guides/eldt-class-c).

---

# Class B CDL: What It Is, What You Can Drive, and How to Get One

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/class-b-cdl
Updated: 2026-11-16

**A Class B CDL lets you drive a single vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of 26,001 lbs or more, or such a vehicle towing a trailer of 10,000 lbs GVWR or less** (49 CFR 383.91). Think dump trucks, box trucks, cement mixers, garbage trucks, and city or school buses (with the P and S endorsements). First-time Class B applicants must complete Class B ELDT theory and behind-the-wheel training before the skills test.

## What can you drive with a Class B CDL?

- Straight trucks and box trucks 26,001+ lbs GVWR
- Dump trucks and cement mixers
- Garbage and recycling trucks
- Delivery trucks for beverages, building supplies, and furniture
- Tow trucks (heavy-duty)
- City, transit, and tour buses (with P endorsement)
- School buses (with P and S endorsements)
- Class C vehicles, with required endorsements

You **can't** drive a tractor-trailer or tow a trailer over 10,000 lbs with a Class B.

## Class B CDL requirements

- Age 18 (intrastate) or 21 (interstate)
- DOT medical certificate
- CLP with General Knowledge (and Air Brakes, if your vehicle has air brakes)
- 14-day CLP holding period
- **[Class B ELDT](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-b)** theory (80%+) and BTW from registered providers
- Skills test in a representative Class B vehicle

## Class B ELDT

Class B theory follows Appendix B to Part 380: basic operation, safe operating procedures, advanced operating practices, vehicle systems and malfunctions, and non-driving activities. It skips combination-vehicle topics like coupling. Our Class B course is 29 lessons, about 13 hours. Bus drivers also need [Passenger (P)](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-passenger-p-endorsement) ELDT, and school bus drivers need [School Bus (S)](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-school-bus-s-endorsement) ELDT too.

## Class B CDL jobs

Local delivery, construction, waste management, municipal public works, utilities, transit, school transportation, and charter or tour buses. Class B jobs are often local with home time every night.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is a Class B CDL worth it?
For local work and bus driving, yes. If you might want tractor-trailer work later, consider Class A now: it covers Class B vehicles too, and upgrading later requires ELDT again.

### Do school bus drivers need a Class B CDL?
Most full-size school buses require a Class B with P and S endorsements. Smaller buses under 26,001 lbs may require Class C with P and S.

### Can I upgrade from Class B to Class A later?
Yes, but an upgrade requires Class A ELDT before the Class A skills test. See [Class B to Class A upgrade](/guides/class-b-to-class-a-upgrade).

### How much does Class B ELDT cost?
Our online Class B theory course is $119.99 (regular $159.99).

---

# How to Upgrade from a Class B to a Class A CDL

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/class-b-to-class-a-upgrade
Updated: 2026-11-16

**To upgrade from Class B to Class A, you need a Class A commercial learner's permit (pass the Combination Vehicles test, plus Air Brakes if you haven't), Class A ELDT theory and behind-the-wheel training from FMCSA-registered providers, a 14-day CLP holding period, and a passing Class A skills test.** The federal ELDT rule specifically lists a Class B to Class A upgrade as entry-level training, so you can't skip it, even with years of Class B experience.

## Step-by-step upgrade

1. **Check your medical certificate** is current.
2. **Pass the Class A knowledge tests** your state requires, typically Combination Vehicles (and Air Brakes if your Class B has an air brake restriction).
3. **Get your Class A CLP** and hold it for at least 14 days.
4. **Complete Class A upgrade theory** with a registered provider. Our [Class B to A Upgrade course](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-b-to-a-upgrade) is about 12 hours, focused on combination-vehicle knowledge.
5. **Complete Class A BTW training** with a registered provider: range (coupling, uncoupling, backing with a trailer) and public road in a combination vehicle.
6. **Take the Class A skills test.** Your state checks the TPR for your Class A ELDT records first.

## Why experienced drivers still need ELDT

49 CFR 380.609 requires ELDT for anyone "upgrading" from a Class B to a Class A CDL. The rule is about the license class, not experience. Your Class B experience helps you move through BTW faster, since there's no minimum hours and your instructor certifies proficiency.

## Upgrade course vs full Class A course

| | B-to-A Upgrade | Full Class A |
|---|---|---|
| Best for | Current Class B holders | New drivers |
| Duration (ours) | ~12 hours, 22 lessons | ~15 hours, 30 lessons |
| Price (ours) | $99.99 | $129.99 |
| Focus | Combination vehicles, coupling, handling | Complete Class A curriculum from scratch |

## What it costs to upgrade

Theory: $99.99 here. BTW for experienced Class B drivers is often shorter, so cheaper, than for brand-new drivers. Add state fees for the CLP, knowledge tests, skills test, and license upgrade.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need ELDT to upgrade from B to A if I got my Class B before 2022?
Yes. The exemption for pre-February 7, 2022 licenses only covers the class you already held. A Class A is a new class for you.

### Can I keep driving my Class B truck while I train?
Yes. Your Class B CDL stays valid. The Class A CLP only adds permission to practice in combination vehicles with a qualified Class A driver.

### Do I need to retake the general knowledge test?
Usually not, if your Class B is valid. States typically require only the Combination Vehicles test (and Air Brakes if needed), but check your state's rules.

### Does upgrading change my endorsements?
Your existing endorsements generally carry over. Adding new ones (like hazmat) is separate.

---

# DOT Physical and Medical Card for CDL Drivers

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/dot-physical-medical-card
Updated: 2026-11-16

**A DOT physical is a medical exam by a certified medical examiner on the FMCSA National Registry that checks whether you can safely drive a commercial vehicle.** It covers vision (at least 20/40 in each eye, corrected or not), hearing, blood pressure, a urinalysis, and a review of your health history. If you pass, you get a medical examiner's certificate valid for up to 24 months (less if you have a condition that needs monitoring). Exams commonly cost about $75 to $150.

## What the DOT physical checks

| Area | Standard (summary) |
|---|---|
| Vision | At least 20/40 in each eye and both eyes together, with or without correction; 70° field of vision in each eye; recognize red, green, amber |
| Hearing | Perceive a forced whisper at 5 feet, or pass an audiometric test |
| Blood pressure | Below 140/90 for a full 2-year card; higher readings may mean a shorter card or disqualification until controlled |
| Urinalysis | Screens for protein, blood, and sugar (not a drug test) |
| Health history | Heart, lung, neurological, diabetes, sleep disorders, medications |

A **drug test** is separate. Employers require a pre-employment DOT drug test for CDL jobs.

## Conditions that need extra steps

- **Insulin-treated diabetes:** allowed with a treating clinician's assessment form; the card may be limited to 12 months.
- **Sleep apnea:** examiners may require testing or proof of CPAP compliance.
- **Vision in one eye:** FMCSA has an alternative vision standard with specialist evaluation.
- **Hearing loss:** hearing exemptions exist for some drivers.
- **Seizure history:** specific rules and possible exemption programs.

Bring medication lists and specialist notes to avoid delays.

## How long is a DOT medical card good for?

Up to **24 months**. The examiner may issue a shorter certificate (for example 3, 6, or 12 months) to monitor high blood pressure or other conditions. You must keep a valid certificate to keep your CDL privileges for non-excepted interstate driving.

## How results reach your state

FMCSA has moved to electronic transmission of medical certification: certified examiners report results to FMCSA, which shares them with state licensing agencies. Keep a copy of your certificate anyway, and check with your state on whether you still need to self-certify your driving type or submit paperwork.

## Finding a certified examiner

Only examiners on the [FMCSA National Registry](https://nationalregistry.fmcsa.dot.gov/) can perform DOT physicals. Search by ZIP code. Occupational health clinics, urgent care centers, and chiropractors are common registered examiners.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need a DOT physical before my CDL permit?
Yes. Most states require a valid medical examiner's certificate (and self-certification of your driving type) before issuing a CLP.

### Is the DOT physical a drug test?
No. The physical includes a urinalysis for medical screening only. DOT drug tests are separate and usually required by employers.

### Can I fail a DOT physical for high blood pressure?
At 180/110 or higher you can't be certified until it's controlled. Between 140/90 and 180/110 you may receive a shorter certificate.

### Does ELDT require a medical card?
ELDT theory doesn't. You'll need the medical certificate for your CLP, which you need for behind-the-wheel training on public roads.

---

# Doubles and Triples Endorsement (T): Requirements and Test

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/doubles-triples-endorsement
Updated: 2026-11-16

**The T endorsement lets a Class A CDL holder pull double or triple trailers.** You get it by passing your state's doubles/triples knowledge test; there's no skills test, and the federal ELDT rule doesn't apply to the T endorsement. Doubles are common in LTL freight; triples are only legal on certain highways in some states.

## T endorsement requirements

- A Class A CDL (or Class A CLP while training)
- Passing score on the doubles/triples knowledge test (commonly about 20 questions, 80% to pass)
- State endorsement fee

No ELDT and no skills test are federally required, though employers that run doubles usually provide on-the-job training.

## What's on the doubles/triples test

- Coupling and uncoupling a second or third trailer, including converter dollies
- Inspecting the extra connections: air lines, electrical lines, safety chains, pintle hooks
- Checking air flow to the last trailer
- Crack-the-whip effect and rearward amplification
- Rollover risk and the importance of a light trailer in the rear
- Managing space, following distance, and turning with multiple trailers

## Where doubles and triples are used

Double "pup" trailers (about 28 feet each) are a staple of less-than-truckload (LTL) carriers. Triples are permitted on certain routes, mostly in western and some midwestern states, and on specific toll roads. Rules on lengths and routes vary by state.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need ELDT for a doubles/triples endorsement?
No. Federal ELDT covers Class A, Class B, H, P, and S only. Your Class A ELDT already covers combination-vehicle fundamentals.

### Can I get a T endorsement with a Class B CDL?
No. Pulling doubles or triples requires a Class A CDL.

### Is the T endorsement worth getting?
If you want LTL work, yes. It's inexpensive, quick to add, and many LTL carriers require it.

### Can I add T to my CLP?
Only P, S, and N can be placed on a CLP, so T is added once you hold your Class A CDL. You can usually take the knowledge test with your other permit tests.

---

# ELDT Certificate: How Certification Works and How to Verify It

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/eldt-certificate
Updated: 2026-11-16

**ELDT "certification" is an electronic record your training provider submits to the FMCSA Training Provider Registry (TPR), not a paper card you hand to the DMV.** After you pass the theory assessment with 80% or higher (or complete BTW), the provider must submit your certification by midnight of the second business day. Your state licensing agency pulls that record before your skills test or H knowledge test. Many providers, including ours, also give you a downloadable certificate of completion for your own records.

## What gets reported to the TPR

Under 49 CFR 380.717, the provider's electronic certification includes:

- Your full name, driver's license number, and state of licensure
- The training type completed (Class A, Class B, P, S, or H; theory or BTW)
- The date you completed the training
- For theory, confirmation that you passed the assessment (minimum 80%)
- The provider's name and TPR identification number

The record then becomes available to your state driver licensing agency (SDLA) when it checks before testing.

## Paper certificate vs TPR record

| | Certificate of completion | TPR certification record |
|---|---|---|
| Who creates it | Your training provider | Your training provider, submitted to FMCSA |
| Format | PDF you can download or print | Electronic record in the federal registry |
| Who uses it | You and your employer | Your state licensing agency |
| Required to test? | No | Yes |

Keep your certificate as proof for employers and in case you need to follow up, but remember the state relies on the electronic record.

## Why your information must match your license

If the name or license number you entered doesn't match your driver's license or CLP exactly, the state may not find your record. When you enroll:

- Use your full legal name as printed on your license or CLP
- Double-check your license number and issuing state
- If you get a CLP after starting theory, make sure your provider has the license number your state will look up

## How to check that your ELDT was submitted

Only registered providers can submit or view driver records in the TPR; drivers cannot enter or edit records themselves. To confirm:

1. **Ask your provider** for confirmation of the submission date.
2. **Wait at least two business days** after completion.
3. **Ask your state licensing agency** when you schedule your test whether your ELDT record is visible.

## What to do if your state can't find your ELDT

1. Confirm with your provider that the record was submitted and that the name and license number are correct. Providers can correct errors in records they submitted.
2. Confirm the training type matches the test (for example, Class A theory for a Class A skills test).
3. For Class A, B, P, and S, confirm **both** theory and BTW have been reported.
4. If the provider was removed from the registry, contact your state licensing agency right away about your options.

## Does an ELDT certificate expire?

FMCSA's Training Provider Registry FAQs do not set an expiration date for ELDT certifications. Your commercial learner's permit does expire, so schedule training and testing within its validity. See [how long ELDT results are valid](/guides/how-long-is-eldt-training).

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need to bring my ELDT certificate to the DMV?
Usually not. Your state checks the electronic record in the Training Provider Registry. Bring your certificate anyway in case the clerk asks, but the TPR record is what qualifies you to test.

### How do I get my ELDT certificate?
At ELDT Training you can download your certificate of completion right after you pass the final assessment. We also submit your completion to the TPR.

### Can I see my ELDT record in the TPR myself?
The registry's driver records are accessed by training providers and state licensing agencies. Drivers can search the public registry for providers but can't edit training records.

### Is ELDT certification the same as a CDL?
No. ELDT certification qualifies you to take the CDL skills test (or H knowledge test). You still have to pass the state test to get your CDL or endorsement.

---

# Do You Need ELDT for a Class C CDL?

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/eldt-class-c
Updated: 2026-11-16

**No ELDT is required just to get a Class C CDL**, because the federal ELDT rule covers Class A and Class B. But a Class C CDL is only needed when a vehicle carries 16+ passengers or placarded hazmat, so Class C drivers almost always need an endorsement, and **first-time P, S, or H endorsements do require ELDT**. A Class C passenger-van driver needs P endorsement ELDT; a Class C hazmat delivery driver needs hazmat ELDT.

## What is a Class C CDL?

Under 49 CFR 383.91, Class C covers any single vehicle or combination that doesn't meet the Class A or Class B weight definitions but is either:

- **Designed to transport 16 or more passengers**, including the driver, or
- **Used to transport hazardous materials** in a quantity requiring placards (or certain select agents and toxins)

Typical Class C jobs: large passenger vans and small shuttle buses, smaller school or activity buses, and lighter hazmat delivery trucks (propane, chemicals) under 26,001 lbs.

## How ELDT applies to Class C

| Class C situation | ELDT required? | Course |
|---|---|---|
| Class C CDL with no endorsements | No (federal) | — |
| Class C + first-time Passenger (P) | **Yes** | [Passenger (P) ELDT](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-passenger-p-endorsement) |
| Class C + first-time School Bus (S) | **Yes** (plus P) | [School Bus (S) ELDT](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-school-bus-s-endorsement) |
| Class C + first-time Hazmat (H) | **Yes** | [Hazmat (H) ELDT](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-hazmat-h-endorsement) |
| Class C + Tanker (N) | No (federal) | Optional [N training](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-tanker-n-endorsement) |

For P and S, ELDT includes theory plus behind-the-wheel training in a representative vehicle. For H, theory alone is enough.

## Class C vs Class B

If the vehicle has a GVWR of 26,001 lbs or more, it's Class B (or A), not Class C, and Class B ELDT applies. A full-size transit bus or most school buses fall into Class B. Smaller 15- to 24-passenger buses under 26,001 lbs are often Class C.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I take Class C ELDT online?
There's no separate "Class C ELDT." You take the endorsement course you need (P, S, or H). Theory for all three can be completed online; P and S also need behind-the-wheel training.

### Do I need a CDL to drive a 15-passenger van?
A van designed for 15 or fewer passengers including the driver generally doesn't require a CDL. Vehicles designed for 16 or more (including the driver) do. Check the manufacturer's rated seating capacity.

### Is Class C the same as a regular driver's license?
No. In many states a regular non-commercial license is also called "Class C," which causes confusion. A Class C CDL is a commercial license issued under federal CDL standards.

### Do I need a medical card for a Class C CDL?
Most Class C CDL holders operating in interstate commerce need a DOT medical examiner's certificate. See [DOT physical and medical card](/guides/dot-physical-medical-card).

---

# How Much Does ELDT Training Cost?

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/eldt-cost
Updated: 2026-11-16

**Online ELDT theory training typically costs about $50 to $150, depending on the license or endorsement.** At ELDT Training, Class A theory is $129.99, Class B is $119.99, the Class B to A upgrade is $99.99, Hazmat (H) is $69.99, and Passenger (P) and School Bus (S) are $59.99 each. Behind-the-wheel training, required for Class A, B, P, and S, is priced separately and is usually the larger expense, often bundled into CDL school tuition.

## ELDT theory prices at ELDT Training

| Course | Price | Regular price | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Class A ELDT](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-a) | **$129.99** | $159.99 | 15 hours |
| [Class B ELDT](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-b) | **$119.99** | $159.99 | 13 hours |

| [Passenger (P) Endorsement](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-passenger-p-endorsement) | **$59.99** | $99.99 | 6 hours |

| [Tanker (N) Endorsement](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-tanker-n-endorsement) | **$49.99** | $99.99 | 1 hour |

Every price includes the final assessment and reporting your completion to the FMCSA Training Provider Registry. There is no extra "TPR submission fee."

## What behind-the-wheel training costs

Behind-the-wheel (BTW) training needs a truck or bus, fuel, insurance, a range, and an instructor, so it costs more than theory. Pricing varies widely by region and provider:

- **Hourly BTW** at independent schools is often priced per hour of truck time.
- **BTW packages** for Class A commonly run from roughly $1,500 to $5,000+ depending on how much practice you need.
- **Full CDL school programs** (theory + BTW + test prep) commonly range from about $3,000 to $10,000.
- **Company-sponsored training** may cost nothing upfront in exchange for a work commitment. See [paid CDL training](/guides/paid-cdl-training).

Because theory and BTW can come from different registered providers, many drivers save money by completing theory online first and then buying only the BTW they need.

## Other costs on the road to a CDL

| Item | Typical range |
|---|---|
| DOT medical exam | About $75 to $150 |
| CLP and CDL state fees | Varies by state (often $50 to $300 combined) |
| Skills test fee or third-party tester | Varies by state, sometimes $100 to $300+ |
| Truck rental for the skills test (if not provided by school) | Varies |
| TSA threat assessment (H or X only) | Under $100, paid to TSA's enrollment provider |

Full breakdown: [How much does it cost to get a CDL?](/guides/how-much-does-it-cost-to-get-a-cdl)

## Why are some online ELDT courses $25?

You'll see ads for very cheap ELDT. Before buying, check:

- Is the provider currently listed on the [Training Provider Registry](/guides/training-provider-registry) for your training type? Training from a removed provider is invalid.
- Does the price include the final assessment and TPR reporting?
- Is there a real support phone number and refund policy?
- Is it the full curriculum for your license class, or an add-on module?

## Ways to save on ELDT

- **Do theory online** and shop BTW separately.
- **Ask your employer.** Many carriers, school districts, transit agencies, and municipalities reimburse ELDT.
- **Check workforce programs.** WIOA-funded programs and community colleges sometimes cover CDL training costs. See [free ELDT training](/guides/free-eldt-training).
- **Bundle endorsements** you'll need anyway (for example, P and S for school bus jobs) so you only take the skills test trip once.
- **Veterans** may be eligible for the military skills test waiver, which also exempts them from ELDT.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much is ELDT training online?
Online ELDT theory usually costs about $50 to $150. Our prices range from $49.99 (Tanker N) to $129.99 (Class A and X endorsement).

### Is ELDT included in CDL school tuition?
Usually. Most CDL schools registered on the TPR include both theory and BTW. If you already finished theory online with another registered provider, ask the school whether it offers a BTW-only price.

### Do I have to pay for ELDT again if I fail the CDL skills test?
No. Your ELDT record stays in the TPR. Failing the state skills test does not erase your training; you just retest according to your state's rules (and pay any retest fee).

### Can my employer pay for my ELDT course?
Yes. Employers can purchase courses for drivers. Contact us at (866) 429-6742 for help enrolling multiple drivers.

### Is the hazmat ELDT course cheaper than Class A?
Yes. Hazmat theory is shorter (about 5 hours) and costs $69.99 at ELDT Training. You'll also pay TSA for the security threat assessment.
