# ELDT Curriculum: What Class A, B, H, P, and S Training Covers

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/eldt-curriculum
Updated: 2026-11-16

**The ELDT curriculum is set by FMCSA in the appendices to 49 CFR Part 380:** Appendix A (Class A), B (Class B), C (Passenger), D (School Bus), and E (Hazmat). Class A and B theory each have five units: Basic Operation, Safe Operating Procedures, Advanced Operating Practices, Vehicle Systems and Reporting Malfunctions, and Non-Driving Activities. Providers must cover every topic, and you must score at least 80% on the theory assessment.

## Class A and Class B theory: the five units

### Unit 1: Basic Operation
Orientation to the CMV and the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations, control systems and dashboard, pre-trip and post-trip inspections, basic control, shifting and operating transmissions, backing and docking, and (Class A only) coupling and uncoupling combination vehicles.

### Unit 2: Safe Operating Procedures
Visual search, communication and signaling, distracted driving, speed management, space management, night operation, and extreme driving conditions such as ice, heavy rain, high winds, mountains, and desert heat. Seat belt use under 49 CFR 392.16 is emphasized.

### Unit 3: Advanced Operating Practices
Hazard perception, skid control and recovery, jackknifing and other emergencies (brake failure, tire blowouts, evasive steering), and railroad-highway grade crossings.

### Unit 4: Vehicle Systems and Reporting Malfunctions
Identifying and diagnosing malfunctions, roadside inspections, and maintenance responsibilities, including driver vehicle inspection reports.

### Unit 5: Non-Driving Activities
Handling and documenting cargo, environmental compliance, hours of service, fatigue and wellness awareness, post-crash procedures, external communications (dispatch, shippers, law enforcement), whistleblower and coercion protections, trip planning, drugs and alcohol rules, and medical requirements.

## How Class A and Class B differ

| Topic | Class A | Class B |
|---|---|---|
| Coupling and uncoupling | Yes | No |
| Combination vehicle handling and off-tracking | Yes | Limited |
| Range BTW skills | Straight-line, alley dock, offset backing, parallel parking, coupling/uncoupling | Straight-line, alley dock, offset backing, parallel parking |
| Public-road BTW | Yes | Yes |

Completing Class A ELDT also qualifies you to take the Class B skills test, but not the reverse.

## Behind-the-wheel curriculum (Class A and B)

**Range:** vehicle inspection, straight-line backing, alley dock backing (45/90 degree), offset backing, parallel parking (sight side and blind side), and coupling/uncoupling (Class A).

**Public road:** vehicle controls (turns, lane changes, curves at highway speeds, entering and exiting the interstate), shifting, backing and docking, visual search, communication, speed and space management, safe driver behavior, hazard perception, railroad crossings, and, where conditions allow, night operation and extreme conditions.

## Passenger (P) curriculum: Appendix C

Vehicle orientation, pre-trip/en route/post-trip inspections, fueling, idling, post-crash and other emergency procedures, baggage and cargo management, passenger management and safety awareness, hours of service, seat belt and safety, railroad crossings, navigating highways and tunnels, security awareness, roadside inspections, and vehicle maintenance. BTW covers maneuvering a passenger vehicle on a range and/or public road.

## School Bus (S) curriculum: Appendix D

Danger zones and use of mirrors, loading and unloading, emergency exit and evacuation, railroad-highway grade crossings, student management, antilock braking systems, and special safety considerations. BTW covers school bus maneuvers, loading and unloading procedures, and railroad crossings on a range and/or public road.

## Hazmat (H) curriculum: Appendix E

Basic and operational hazmat requirements, reporting crashes and releases, tunnels and railroad crossings, loading and unloading, cargo segregation, hazmat on passenger vehicles, bulk packages (cargo tanks, portable tanks), operating emergency equipment, emergency response procedures, engine (fueling), tire checks, routes and route planning, and hazardous materials safety permits. Hazmat is theory only.

## How our courses map to the curriculum

Our [Class A course](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-a) organizes the five units into 30 lessons, [Class B](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-b) into 29, and [Hazmat](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-hazmat-h-endorsement) into 13, each ending with a practice exam and final assessment.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is the ELDT curriculum the same as the CDL manual?
They overlap but aren't the same. Your state CDL manual prepares you for state knowledge tests. The ELDT curriculum is FMCSA's required training content and includes non-driving topics like whistleblower protections, wellness, and trip planning that the manual covers lightly or not at all.

### Do providers have to teach every topic?
Yes. Registered providers must cover all topics in the applicable appendix. There's no minimum time per topic.

### Where can I read the official curriculum?
The appendices to 49 CFR Part 380 are published on eCFR. Links are in the sources below.

### Does the curriculum prepare me for the skills test?
Theory teaches the knowledge behind the skills test (inspection items, backing techniques, safe driving practices). BTW training is where you practice the actual maneuvers.

---

# ELDT Exemptions: Who Doesn't Need Entry-Level Driver Training

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/eldt-exemptions
Updated: 2026-11-16

**You don't need ELDT if you already held the CDL class or endorsement before February 7, 2022, if you got your CLP before that date and obtain your CDL before the CLP (or renewed CLP) expires, or if you are excepted from the CDL skills test**, such as qualifying military drivers using the skills-test waiver under 49 CFR 383.77. ELDT also isn't required for the Tanker (N) or Doubles/Triples (T) endorsements or for removing L, Z, or E restrictions.

## Exemption 1: You held the license or endorsement before February 7, 2022

ELDT is not retroactive. If you held a valid Class A or Class B CDL, or an H, P, or S endorsement, issued before February 7, 2022, you don't need ELDT for that same license class or endorsement.

**Lapsed licenses:** Under 49 CFR 380.603, drivers who previously held a CDL issued before February 7, 2022 and are re-obtaining a CDL of the same class are not subject to ELDT, even if the CDL lapsed. Your state may still require you to retake tests.

## Exemption 2: You had a CLP before February 7, 2022

If you obtained a commercial learner's permit before February 7, 2022, you are not subject to ELDT **as long as you obtain your CDL before that CLP or renewed CLP expires**. If your permit expired and you have to get a new one, ELDT applies. Since CLPs last at most about a year, this exemption has largely run out.

## Exemption 3: You're excepted from the CDL skills test

The ELDT rule didn't create new exceptions; it follows the existing CDL skills-test exceptions. You're not subject to ELDT if you're applying under:

- **Military skills-test waiver** (49 CFR 383.77) for current or recently separated service members who operated equivalent military vehicles
- Exceptions in 49 CFR 383.3(c), (d), and (h), such as certain farm, firefighter, and military-vehicle operator exceptions where the state doesn't require a CDL
- **Restricted CDLs** under 49 CFR 383.3(e) through (g) for certain farm-related service industries and similar seasonal operations, where states issue them

## Exemption 4: Restriction removals

Removing these restrictions does not require ELDT:

- **L or Z** (air brake restrictions)
- **E** (no manual transmission)

For restriction removal under 49 CFR 383.135(b)(7), check your state's process. Most require a skills test in the right vehicle. See [CDL restrictions](/guides/cdl-restrictions).

## Not exempt: endorsements and upgrades people often miss

| Situation | ELDT needed? |
|---|---|
| Class B holder upgrading to Class A | **Yes**, Class A training |
| Class A holder adding first-time hazmat | **Yes**, H theory |
| CDL holder adding first-time P or S | **Yes**, P or S theory + BTW |
| Adding Tanker (N) | No (federal) |
| Adding Doubles/Triples (T) | No |
| Class C holder adding first-time H, P, or S | **Yes**, for that endorsement |
| Class A holder who wants to drive Class B vehicles | No |

## Military drivers: ELDT and the skills test waiver

Service members and veterans who qualify for their state's military skills test waiver are excepted from the skills test, and therefore from ELDT, for that license class. If you don't qualify for the waiver (for example, too much time has passed since separation), ELDT applies like any other new driver. Many states also offer military knowledge-test waivers; check your state's program.

## Frequently asked questions

### Am I grandfathered from ELDT?
If you held the same CDL class or endorsement before February 7, 2022, yes. Getting a new class or endorsement for the first time (for example, upgrading B to A or adding hazmat) still requires ELDT for that new class or endorsement.

### My CDL expired years ago. Do I need ELDT?
Under 49 CFR 380.603, if your earlier CDL was issued before February 7, 2022 and you're re-obtaining the same class, ELDT doesn't apply. Your state may still require you to retest.

### Do farmers need ELDT?
Farmers who qualify for a state's farm exception from the CDL aren't getting a CDL, so ELDT doesn't apply. If a farmer gets a regular Class A or B CDL, ELDT applies.

### Do I need ELDT to transfer my CDL to a new state?
No. Transferring an existing CDL of the same class to a new state of residence is not a first-time CDL.

---

# ELDT for Employers and Fleets: What You Need to Know

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/eldt-for-employers
Updated: 2026-11-16

**Employers don't take ELDT themselves, but every new hire getting a first-time Class A or B CDL, a B-to-A upgrade, or a first-time H, P, or S endorsement must complete ELDT with registered providers before testing.** Many fleets outsource theory to an online provider and deliver behind-the-wheel training in-house after registering their own BTW program on the FMCSA Training Provider Registry. Either way, training must come from providers active on the registry.

## Common employer setups

| Setup | How it works | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Fully outsourced | Send hires to a CDL school for theory + BTW | Small fleets, occasional hires |
| Online theory + in-house BTW | Buy online theory seats; register your own BTW program | Fleets with trainers and equipment |
| Fully in-house | Register as a provider for theory and BTW | Large fleets with training departments |
| Hire-after-CDL | Hire only drivers who already completed ELDT | Fleets without training capacity |

## Registering as a BTW provider

To deliver BTW in-house, you register each training location on the TPR and self-certify that you meet the requirements: qualified BTW instructors, representative vehicles in safe operating condition, range facilities that allow all required maneuvers, a curriculum covering every BTW topic, and compliance with any state requirements where training occurs. You must then report each driver's BTW completion by midnight of the second business day.

## Why online theory makes sense for fleets

- **No classroom or instructor time** for theory
- **New hires start immediately**, even before their CLP
- **Consistent curriculum** across locations
- **Low cost per driver:** $129.99 Class A, $119.99 Class B, $59.99 to $69.99 endorsements here
- **Documented completion** reported to the TPR

Contact us at (866) 429-6742 or info@eldttraining.us to enroll multiple drivers.

## Compliance checklist for employers

- Verify any outside provider is **active on the TPR** before sending drivers
- Keep records of each driver's ELDT completions (certificate and provider confirmation)
- Remember ELDT applies to **endorsements** too: a current driver adding first-time hazmat, passenger, or school bus needs ELDT for it
- Watch for FMCSA **notices of proposed removal** if you're a registered provider, and fix deficiencies quickly
- Make sure new hires meet the **English language proficiency** requirement

## School districts and transit agencies

New school bus drivers typically need Class B, P, and S ELDT. Many districts register as BTW providers and buy online theory for all three. See [school bus endorsement](/guides/school-bus-endorsement).

## Frequently asked questions

### Can employers buy ELDT courses for drivers?
Yes. Employers can purchase courses and provide logins to drivers. Each driver's completion is reported individually to the TPR under the driver's license information.

### Does an existing driver need ELDT to add an endorsement?
Only for first-time H, P, or S endorsements (and B-to-A upgrades). N and T don't require ELDT.

### Can our trainers deliver theory too?
Yes, if your organization registers as a theory provider and meets the theory instructor and curriculum requirements. Many fleets find outsourcing theory simpler.

### What happens to our hires if our outside school is removed from the TPR?
Training delivered after the removal date is invalid. Verify providers before enrolling drivers and monitor their status.

---

# ELDT Training Requirements: Who Needs It and What's Required

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/eldt-requirements
Updated: 2026-11-16

**Under the federal ELDT rule (49 CFR Part 380), you must complete entry-level driver training from an FMCSA-registered provider before testing if you are getting a first-time Class A or Class B CDL, upgrading from Class B to Class A, or getting a first-time H, P, or S endorsement.** Theory training requires an 80% score on the assessment. Class A, Class B, P, and S also require behind-the-wheel training. There are no minimum hours, and your provider must report completion to the Training Provider Registry before your state will test you.

## Requirement 1: Who must complete ELDT

The trigger is the license or endorsement you are applying for, not your job or employer. Under 49 CFR 380.609, ELDT is required for an individual who:

- Applies for a **Class A or Class B CDL for the first time**
- Applies to **upgrade a Class B CDL to a Class A CDL**
- Applies for a **Hazardous Materials (H), Passenger (P), or School Bus (S) endorsement for the first time**

Not covered: the Tanker (N) endorsement, the Doubles/Triples (T) endorsement, and removing restrictions such as the air brake (L/Z) or manual transmission (E) restriction. A first-time Class C CDL by itself does not trigger ELDT, but adding a P, S, or H endorsement to a Class C does. See [ELDT for Class C](/guides/eldt-class-c).

## Requirement 2: Train with a registered provider

All ELDT must be delivered by a provider listed on the [FMCSA Training Provider Registry (TPR)](/guides/training-provider-registry). Providers self-certify that they meet the curriculum, instructor, facility, and vehicle requirements, and FMCSA can remove providers that do not comply. Training received from a provider after it has been removed from the registry is not valid.

You may use **different providers for theory and behind-the-wheel**. Both must be registered, and each reports its own portion.

## Requirement 3: Complete the theory curriculum and score 80%

Each training type has its own curriculum in the appendices to Part 380:

| Training type | Curriculum |
|---|---|
| Class A CDL | Appendix A |
| Class B CDL | Appendix B |
| Passenger (P) endorsement | Appendix C |
| School Bus (S) endorsement | Appendix D |
| Hazardous Materials (H) endorsement | Appendix E |

The provider must cover every topic in the curriculum. You must score **at least 80% overall** on the written or electronic theory assessment. There is no minimum number of classroom hours. Online delivery is allowed. Learn what's covered in our [ELDT curriculum guide](/guides/eldt-curriculum).

## Requirement 4: Complete behind-the-wheel training (A, B, P, S)

Behind-the-wheel (BTW) training must take place in a representative vehicle for the license class or endorsement, with a qualified BTW instructor.

- **Class A and Class B:** both range training (for example, backing, docking, and coupling for Class A) and public-road training.
- **P and S endorsements:** range and/or public-road training specific to passenger vehicles and school buses.
- **H endorsement:** no BTW requirement.

BTW has no minimum hours. Completion is based on the instructor's assessment of your proficiency in every required skill. FMCSA does not allow driving simulators to substitute for BTW training. Both portions of BTW (range and public road) must be delivered by the same provider.

## Requirement 5: Qualified instructors

ELDT instructors generally must hold a CDL of the same or higher class with any needed endorsements and have at least two years of experience driving a CMV requiring that CDL, or at least two years as a BTW instructor. Online theory content must be prepared and delivered by instructors who meet the federal definition of a theory instructor. States may add their own instructor licensing rules for in-person training.

## Requirement 6: Reporting to the TPR

After you complete a portion of training, the provider must electronically submit your training certification to the TPR **by midnight of the second business day**. The record includes your name, driver's license number and state, the training type, completion date, and the provider's TPR number.

## Requirement 7: State verification before testing

Your state driver licensing agency (SDLA) must confirm the TPR record before it administers:

- The **Class A or Class B skills test**
- The **P or S skills test**
- The **H knowledge test**

The state may schedule your test in advance, but it cannot give the test until the training record is available.

## What ELDT does not require

- **No minimum hours** for theory or BTW.
- **No required order.** You can do theory and BTW in any order, though BTW must be finished before the skills test.
- **No CLP before theory.** You can start theory before you have a commercial learner's permit.
- **No ELDT for N or T endorsements**, or for restriction removals.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are ELDT requirements the same in every state?
The federal requirements are the same everywhere and every state uses the same Training Provider Registry. States may add requirements, especially for in-person BTW training delivered within their borders, so check with your state licensing agency.

### Does ELDT require 160 hours of training?
No. Some CDL schools advertise 160-hour programs, but the federal ELDT rule has no minimum hours. Training is complete when you pass the theory assessment with 80% or more and your BTW instructor certifies proficiency.

### Do I need ELDT for a learner's permit?
No. ELDT is not required to get a CLP. It is required before the skills test (Class A, B, P, S) or the H knowledge test.

### Do drivers with military experience need ELDT?
Military personnel who qualify for the skills-test waiver under 49 CFR 383.77 are not subject to ELDT. Check with your state's military CDL waiver program.

### Is ELDT required for an intrastate-only CDL?
Yes. ELDT applies to Class A and Class B CDLs regardless of whether they carry an intrastate (K) restriction.

---

# The ELDT Test: Theory Assessment, Passing Score, and Practice Questions

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/eldt-test
Updated: 2026-11-16

**The ELDT test is the theory assessment at the end of your ELDT course. You must score at least 80% overall to pass.** It's given by your training provider (written or electronic), not by the DMV, and covers the federal curriculum for your license or endorsement. When you pass, the provider reports your completion to the FMCSA Training Provider Registry. It's separate from your state's CDL permit tests.

## ELDT test vs DMV permit test

| | ELDT theory assessment | State CDL knowledge tests |
|---|---|---|
| Given by | Your registered training provider | State licensing agency |
| Passing score | 80% overall | Typically 80% per test |
| Purpose | Proves you completed ELDT theory | Qualifies you for a CLP or endorsement |
| Reported to | FMCSA Training Provider Registry | Your state driver record |
| Required before | Skills test (A, B, P, S) or H knowledge test | CLP issuance |

If you already have your CLP, you've passed the state tests. The ELDT assessment is the additional federally required training check.

## What happens if you fail the ELDT test?

Federal rules require a minimum score of 80% but don't limit retakes. Most providers, including ours, let you review the material and try again. Ask your provider about its retake policy before you enroll.

## Free ELDT practice questions

Test yourself with these questions based on the Class A/B theory curriculum and federal regulations. Answers are below.

1. What is the minimum overall score needed to pass the ELDT theory assessment? (a) 70% (b) 75% (c) 80% (d) 90%
2. Under the property-carrying hours-of-service rules, how many hours may you drive after 10 consecutive hours off duty? (a) 10 (b) 11 (c) 12 (d) 14
3. After how many cumulative hours of driving must a property-carrying driver take a 30-minute break? (a) 4 (b) 6 (c) 8 (d) 10
4. What blood alcohol concentration is the federal limit for CMV drivers? (a) 0.02 (b) 0.04 (c) 0.08 (d) 0.10
5. Buses carrying passengers and vehicles carrying certain hazmat must stop how far from the nearest rail at a railroad crossing? (a) 5 to 15 feet (b) 15 to 50 feet (c) 50 to 100 feet (d) 100 to 200 feet
6. When stopped on a two-lane road, where do you place warning triangles? (a) 10 ft, 50 ft, 100 ft behind (b) 10 ft behind, 100 ft behind, 100 ft ahead (c) 50 ft behind and 50 ft ahead (d) 200 ft behind only
7. Within how many minutes of stopping must warning devices be placed? (a) 5 (b) 10 (c) 15 (d) 30
8. Is using a hand-held mobile phone while driving a CMV allowed? (a) Yes, at low speed (b) Yes, at stop lights (c) No (d) Only for dispatch
9. A common rule for following distance below 40 mph is one second for every how many feet of vehicle length? (a) 5 (b) 10 (c) 20 (d) 40
10. What is the minimum tread depth for tires on a steering axle? (a) 2/32 inch (b) 4/32 inch (c) 6/32 inch (d) 8/32 inch
11. Which ELDT training type requires theory only, with no behind-the-wheel? (a) Class B (b) Passenger (c) School Bus (d) Hazmat
12. By when must a training provider report your completion to the TPR? (a) Same day (b) Midnight of the second business day (c) Within 10 days (d) Within 30 days

**Answers:** 1-c, 2-b, 3-c, 4-b, 5-b, 6-b, 7-b, 8-c, 9-b, 10-b, 11-d, 12-b.

## How to prepare for the ELDT assessment

- Complete every lesson and quiz; don't rush the non-driving units (hours of service, drugs and alcohol, whistleblower rules).
- Use audio playback to review while commuting.
- Retake practice quizzes until you're comfortably above 80%.
- Review the numbers: hours-of-service limits, BAC limits, warning device placement, tire tread depths, railroad crossing distances.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there a free ELDT practice test?
The 12 questions above are a free sample. Our courses include quizzes after lessons and a practice exam before the final assessment.

### Is the ELDT test online?
For online theory courses, yes, the assessment is taken online at the end of the course.

### Are ELDT test answers available as a PDF?
Legitimate providers don't publish their assessment answers. Study the curriculum instead; the assessment checks that you learned it.

### How many questions are on the ELDT test?
FMCSA doesn't set a number. Each provider designs its assessment to cover the full curriculum, and you need 80% overall.

# ELDT Theory vs Behind-the-Wheel Training

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/eldt-theory-vs-behind-the-wheel
Updated: 2026-11-16

**ELDT theory is the knowledge portion (regulations, vehicle systems, safe operating practices) and can be completed online with an 80% passing score. Behind-the-wheel (BTW) training is hands-on driving in a real commercial vehicle with a qualified instructor.** Class A, Class B, Passenger (P), and School Bus (S) require both. The Hazmat (H) endorsement requires theory only. Neither part has minimum hours, they can be done in any order, and they can come from different registered providers.

## Side-by-side comparison

| | Theory training | Behind-the-wheel training |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | Knowledge instruction | Hands-on driving instruction |
| Where | Online or classroom | Range and/or public road, in a representative vehicle |
| Completion standard | 80% overall on theory assessment | Instructor certifies proficiency in every skill |
| Minimum hours | None | None |
| Required for | A, B, B-to-A, H, P, S | A, B, B-to-A, P, S (not H) |
| Simulators allowed? | May be used as a teaching aid | No |
| Typical cost | About $50 to $150 online | Usually the bulk of CDL school tuition |

## What ELDT theory covers

For Class A and Class B, theory follows five units:

1. **Basic operation:** orientation, control systems and dashboard, pre- and post-trip inspections, basic control, shifting, backing and docking, and (Class A) coupling and uncoupling.
2. **Safe operating procedures:** visual search, communication, distracted driving, speed and space management, night operation, extreme driving conditions.
3. **Advanced operating practices:** hazard perception, skid control and recovery, jackknifing and other emergencies, railroad-highway grade crossings.
4. **Vehicle systems and reporting malfunctions:** identifying and diagnosing malfunctions, roadside inspections, maintenance.
5. **Non-driving activities:** handling and documenting cargo, environmental compliance, hours of service, fatigue and wellness, post-crash procedures, external communications, whistleblower and coercion rules, trip planning, drugs and alcohol, medical requirements.

Endorsement theory (H, P, S) covers topics specific to hazmat, passengers, or school buses. See the [ELDT curriculum guide](/guides/eldt-curriculum).

## What behind-the-wheel training covers

**Range training (Class A example):** vehicle inspection, straight-line backing, alley dock backing, offset backing, parallel parking (sight side and blind side), and coupling and uncoupling.

**Public-road training:** vehicle controls in traffic (turns, lane changes, curves, entering and exiting highways), shifting, visual search, communication and signaling, speed and space management, safe driver behavior, hazard perception, railroad crossings, and night or adverse conditions where possible.

Class A and B require **both** range and public-road BTW, and both must come from the same BTW provider. For P and S endorsements, BTW is conducted on a range and/or public road in a passenger vehicle or school bus.

## Which order should you do them in?

FMCSA does not require a specific order. Many drivers do theory first because:

- It is online and can start immediately, even before you have a CLP
- It teaches the inspection steps, terminology, and rules you'll practice in BTW
- It often helps with the CLP knowledge tests

The only timing rule is that **BTW must be finished before your skills test**, and you need a [commercial learner's permit](/guides/cdl-permit-clp) to drive on public roads during BTW.

## Can theory and BTW be from different providers?

Yes. Theory and BTW can be delivered by separate providers, as long as both are on the [Training Provider Registry](/guides/training-provider-registry). Each provider reports its own portion. A common path: online theory from a provider like ELDT Training, then BTW at a local CDL school or with a carrier.

## How BTW is evaluated

There is no hour count. Your BTW instructor must observe you performing every required skill proficiently. Drivers with prior farm, military, or construction equipment experience may finish quickly; brand-new drivers often need more practice. Ask a BTW provider how they price training: by the hour, by package, or by a flat fee to proficiency.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I do behind-the-wheel training online?
No. BTW must take place in a real commercial vehicle with a qualified instructor. FMCSA does not allow driving simulators to replace BTW training.

### Do I need BTW for the hazmat endorsement?
No. The H endorsement is theory only. Your state checks your hazmat theory record before the H knowledge test.

### How many hours of behind-the-wheel training do I need?
The federal rule has no minimum. Your instructor decides when you are proficient. Some states and employers set their own hour requirements.

### Does my CDL school count as both theory and BTW?
If the school is registered on the TPR for both theory and BTW in your training type, yes. Confirm both are listed for the school's location.

### Can I do theory in one state and BTW in another?
Yes. Online theory is not tied to a state. In-person BTW must meet the rules of the state where it is delivered, and your home state may add requirements, so check before you book.

---

# Free ELDT Training: Real Ways to Get ELDT Paid For

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/free-eldt-training
Updated: 2026-11-16

**ELDT only counts if it comes from a provider on the FMCSA Training Provider Registry, and registered providers almost always charge for it.** "Free" ELDT usually means someone else pays: an employer, a carrier with a company-sponsored CDL program, a school district or transit agency, a WIOA workforce grant, or veterans education benefits. Free practice tests and study guides are useful for learning, but they do not satisfy the ELDT requirement.

## Free study materials vs free ELDT

| Resource | Free? | Counts as ELDT? |
|---|---|---|
| State CDL manual | Yes | No |
| Practice tests and flashcards | Often | No |
| YouTube videos | Yes | No |
| Theory from a TPR-registered provider | Usually paid | **Yes** |
| BTW from a TPR-registered provider | Usually paid | **Yes** |

Use free materials to study for your [CDL permit test](/guides/cdl-permit-test), but plan on a registered provider for the training itself.

## Legitimate ways to get ELDT paid for

### 1. Your employer
Many employers reimburse or directly purchase ELDT for new hires: construction companies, municipalities, utilities, waste haulers, beverage distributors, and fuel companies. Ask HR before you enroll. Employers can buy courses for drivers and give you the login.

### 2. Company-sponsored CDL training
Some large carriers train new drivers at no upfront cost in exchange for a work commitment (often around a year). If you leave early, you may owe some or all of the training cost. Read the contract carefully. See [paid CDL training](/guides/paid-cdl-training).

### 3. School districts and transit agencies
School bus contractors, districts, and public transit agencies often pay for the Class B, P, and S training their drivers need, and may pay you while you train.

### 4. WIOA workforce funding
The Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act funds job training through local American Job Centers. CDL training is a common approved program. Funding usually goes to providers on your state's eligible training provider list, so ask your local center which programs qualify.

### 5. Veterans benefits
Veterans may be able to use GI Bill benefits at approved CDL programs. Many veterans qualify for the military skills test waiver, which also exempts them from ELDT for that license class. See [ELDT exemptions](/guides/eldt-exemptions).

### 6. Low-cost online theory
If no one is paying, online theory is the cheapest legitimate option. Our hazmat course is $69.99 and Class A is $129.99. Doing theory online can also cut what you pay a CDL school for BTW.

## Red flags with "free ELDT" offers

- The provider isn't on the [Training Provider Registry](/guides/training-provider-registry)
- They only offer a "certificate" with no final assessment
- They ask for personal information or payment for a "TPR filing fee" separate from training
- The training contract has steep repayment penalties you don't understand

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there free hazmat ELDT training online?
Not usually from registered providers. Your employer may pay. Our hazmat ELDT course is $69.99 and is theory only, so it's the whole ELDT requirement for the H endorsement.

### Do trucking companies pay for ELDT?
Many do, either through company-sponsored CDL schools or by reimbursing new hires. Terms vary, so read any training agreement carefully.

### Can I use free practice tests instead of ELDT?
No. Practice tests can help you pass state knowledge tests, but your state requires a TPR record from a registered provider before the skills test.

### Will my state pay for CDL training?
Some states fund CDL training through workforce grants and community colleges. Contact your local American Job Center.

# Hazmat Endorsement: How to Get Your CDL H Endorsement

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/hazmat-endorsement
Updated: 2026-11-16

**To get a hazmat (H) endorsement: (1) complete hazmat ELDT theory with an FMCSA-registered provider, (2) pass your state's hazmat knowledge test, and (3) pass the TSA security threat assessment (online application, fingerprints, and fee).** You must hold or be getting a CDL, and in practice be at least 21. Hazmat ELDT is theory only, with no behind-the-wheel requirement, so it can be done entirely online. Most drivers get the endorsement within a few weeks, depending on TSA processing.

ELDT required: Yes, theory only
Our course: $69.99, about 5 hours
Knowledge test: Hazmat test (typically ~30 questions)
Security check: TSA threat assessment + fingerprints
TSA approval valid: 5 years

## Who needs a hazmat endorsement?

You need an H endorsement to drive a CMV transporting hazardous materials in a quantity that requires placards under the Hazardous Materials Regulations, or any quantity of certain select agents and toxins. Common hazmat loads include fuel, compressed gases (propane), corrosives, explosives, flammable solids, and radioactive materials.

**How much hazmat can you carry without an endorsement?** If the load doesn't require placards, you don't need the H endorsement. Placards are required for any amount of "Table 1" materials (for example, certain explosives and poison gases) and for 1,001 lbs or more aggregate gross weight of "Table 2" materials. Shippers and carriers determine placarding; when in doubt, don't drive a placarded load without the endorsement.

## Step 1: Complete hazmat ELDT

If you're getting the H endorsement for the first time, you must complete hazmat theory training from a provider on the Training Provider Registry before the knowledge test. The curriculum (Appendix E to Part 380) covers:

- Hazmat basics: the hazardous materials table, shipping papers, marking, labeling, placarding
- Reporting crashes and releases
- Tunnels and railroad crossings
- Loading, unloading, segregation, and securement
- Bulk packages, cargo tanks, portable tanks
- Emergency equipment and emergency response
- Fueling rules and tire checks
- Route planning and hazardous materials safety permits

Our [hazmat ELDT course](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-hazmat-h-endorsement) covers all of it in 13 lessons (about 5 hours) for $69.99. Pass with 80% or higher and we report it to the TPR.

## Step 2: Pass the hazmat knowledge test

After your provider reports your training, your state licensing agency can give you the H knowledge test. It's typically around 30 multiple-choice questions with an 80% passing score (exact format varies by state). Many states require you to retake it when you renew.

## Step 3: Pass the TSA security threat assessment

The Transportation Security Administration's Hazardous Materials Endorsement Threat Assessment Program (HTAPP) is a background check:

1. **Apply online** through TSA's enrollment provider.
2. **Visit an enrollment center** for fingerprints and identity documents.
3. **Pay the fee** (under $100; check TSA for the current amount).
4. **Wait for a determination.** It can take several weeks, so start early. Your state is notified when you're approved.

You must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, or meet other TSA immigration criteria, and not have certain disqualifying criminal offenses. Approval is generally valid for five years.

States differ on whether they want the TSA assessment started before or after the knowledge test. Many drivers start TSA paperwork as soon as they finish ELDT so the background check runs while they study.

## Hazmat endorsement cost

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Hazmat ELDT (online) | $69.99 at ELDT Training |
| TSA threat assessment | Under $100 |
| State knowledge test/endorsement fee | Varies by state |

## Renewing your hazmat endorsement

Renewal doesn't require ELDT. You'll need a new TSA threat assessment (approval is good for up to five years) and, in many states, to pass the hazmat knowledge test again. Start the TSA renewal at least 60 days before your endorsement expires.

## Frequently asked questions

### How long does it take to get a hazmat endorsement?
The ELDT course takes about 5 hours. The longest part is usually TSA processing, which can take several weeks. Many drivers finish within a month.

### Do I need behind-the-wheel training for hazmat?
No. Hazmat ELDT is theory only. There's no hazmat skills test.

### Where can I get fingerprinted for the hazmat endorsement?
At a TSA enrollment center operated by TSA's enrollment provider. You schedule the appointment when you apply online.

### Can I get a hazmat endorsement with a CDL permit?
No. Hazmat can't be added to a CLP. You need a CDL to hold the H endorsement.

### Do I need hazmat ELDT if I had an H endorsement before?
If you held the H endorsement before February 7, 2022, you don't need ELDT to renew it or to get it back.

### Is the hazmat endorsement worth it?
For many drivers, yes. It opens fuel, chemical, and specialized freight jobs that often pay more.

---

# How Long Does It Take to Get a CDL?

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/how-long-does-it-take-to-get-a-cdl
Updated: 2026-11-16

**Most people get a CDL in about 4 to 8 weeks.** The fastest possible path is a little over two weeks, because you must hold your commercial learner's permit for at least 14 days before the skills test. Full-time CDL school programs commonly run 3 to 7 weeks; part-time programs can take a few months. Doing ELDT theory online while you wait out the 14-day CLP period is the easiest way to save time.

## Typical CDL timeline

| Step | Typical time |
|---|---|
| Book and pass DOT physical | 1 to 7 days |
| Study and pass CLP knowledge tests | 1 to 2 weeks |
| Mandatory CLP holding period | 14 days minimum |
| ELDT theory (online) | A few days to 2 weeks (overlaps the 14 days) |
| Behind-the-wheel training | A few days to 3 weeks |
| Schedule and take skills test | Days to several weeks, depending on test-site availability |
| **Total** | **About 4 to 8 weeks** |

## The fastest realistic path

1. **Week 1:** DOT physical, study the CDL manual, pass General Knowledge, Air Brakes, and Combination tests. Start [online ELDT theory](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-a) the same day.
2. **Weeks 2 to 3:** Finish theory while your CLP ages 14 days. Book BTW training and a skills test date.
3. **Weeks 3 to 5:** Complete BTW, then take the skills test.

## What slows people down

- **Skills test appointment backlogs.** Some states have waits of several weeks. Book early; states can schedule your test before training is complete, they just can't administer it until ELDT is in the registry.
- **Failing a knowledge test.** Retest rules and waiting periods vary by state.
- **Medical issues** that require specialist paperwork (sleep apnea, diabetes, vision).
- **BTW availability** at popular schools.
- **Missing documents** for identity, residency, or lawful presence.

## How long is CDL school?

Full-time Class A programs often run 3 to 7 weeks; Class B programs are usually shorter. Part-time evening or weekend programs may take 2 to 4 months. Company-sponsored programs vary, often including a period of supervised driving with a trainer after you get your CDL. See [paid CDL training](/guides/paid-cdl-training).

## How long do endorsements add?

| Endorsement | Extra time |
|---|---|
| Hazmat (H) | ELDT about 5 hours online, plus TSA background check (often a few weeks) |
| Tanker (N) | Knowledge test only |
| Passenger (P) | ELDT about 6 hours online + BTW + skills test |
| School Bus (S) | ELDT about 5 hours online + BTW + skills test |
| Doubles/Triples (T) | Knowledge test only |

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I get a CDL in 2 weeks?
Only barely. You must hold your CLP for 14 days before the skills test, so the absolute minimum is a little over two weeks from CLP to CDL, and that assumes ELDT and BTW are finished within that time and a test slot is available.

### How long does Class B take compared with Class A?
Class B is usually a bit faster because BTW doesn't include coupling or combination-vehicle maneuvers. The 14-day CLP rule still applies.

### How long does the CDL skills test take?
Usually 1.5 to 3 hours for all three parts: pre-trip inspection, basic control, and road test.

### Does ELDT add time to getting a CDL?
Not much if you do theory online during the 14-day CLP period. BTW was always part of learning to drive a truck; ELDT just requires that a registered instructor certify it.

---

# How Long Is ELDT Training, and How Long Are Results Valid?

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/how-long-is-eldt-training
Updated: 2026-11-16

**There is no federal minimum number of hours for ELDT.** Online theory courses are built to take roughly 5 to 15 hours depending on the license or endorsement: about 15 hours for Class A, 13 for Class B, 12 for the B-to-A upgrade, and 5 to 6 for H, P, or S. You finish when you score 80% or higher on the final assessment. Your provider must report completion to the FMCSA Training Provider Registry within two business days. FMCSA's FAQs set no expiration date for ELDT records, but your commercial learner's permit does expire.

## Typical ELDT theory course lengths

| Course | Typical length at ELDT Training | Lessons |
|---|---|---|
| Class A | About 15 hours | 30 |
| Class B | About 13 hours | 29 |
| Class B to A Upgrade | About 12 hours | 22 |
| Passenger (P) | About 6 hours | 18 |
| Hazmat (H) | About 5 hours | 13 |
| School Bus (S) | About 5 hours | 11 |
| X (Hazmat + Tanker) | About 5 hours | 14 |
| Tanker (N) | About 1 hour | 2 + exam |

These are course design estimates. Because ELDT is proficiency-based, you can move faster through material you know and slower through new topics. Most people spread Class A theory over several days or a couple of weeks while working.

## How long does behind-the-wheel training take?

BTW also has no minimum hours. Your instructor decides when you've shown proficiency in each skill. Depending on experience and the program, Class A BTW often takes anywhere from a few days to a few weeks. Full-time CDL school programs (theory + BTW) commonly run 3 to 7 weeks.

## How fast does my completion reach the FMCSA?

Under 49 CFR 380.717, your training provider must submit your training certification to the Training Provider Registry **by midnight of the second business day** after you complete the training. At ELDT Training, we submit as soon as you pass the final assessment. Once submitted, your state driver licensing agency can see the record when it checks before your test.

## How long are ELDT theory results valid?

This is one of the most-searched ELDT questions. Here's what the rules and FMCSA guidance actually say:

- **FMCSA's Training Provider Registry FAQs do not list an expiration date** for ELDT theory or BTW certifications.
- **FMCSA does not require theory and BTW to happen in a particular order.** BTW just has to be complete before the skills test.
- **Your commercial learner's permit does expire.** A CLP is valid for no more than one year under federal rules (states may issue shorter permits with renewal). Plan theory, BTW, and testing within your CLP's validity.
- **Your provider must be active on the TPR when you train.** Training delivered after a provider is removed from the registry is invalid. Training you completed while the provider was listed is a separate question; if your provider is removed, contact your state licensing agency.
- **Some states and employers set their own time limits.** If you plan to wait a long time between theory and testing, confirm with your state licensing agency.

Finish theory first (it's online and quick), then schedule BTW and your skills test while your CLP is valid. Our courses give you a 3-month window to complete the course and 1 year of access to review the material before your tests.

## How long does the whole CDL process take?

With focused effort, many drivers go from zero to CDL in about 4 to 8 weeks: medical exam and CLP (days), 14-day minimum CLP holding period, online theory (days to two weeks), BTW (days to weeks), then the skills test. See [how long it takes to get a CDL](/guides/how-long-does-it-take-to-get-a-cdl).

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I finish ELDT theory in one day?
For short courses like hazmat (about 5 hours), yes. Class A theory is about 15 hours of material, so most people take several sessions. There's no federal minimum, so the pace is up to you as long as you pass with 80% or higher.

### How long do I have to finish the online course?
Our courses include a 3-month completion window and 1 year of access to the training materials.

### Does ELDT need to be renewed?
No. ELDT is a one-time requirement for each license class or endorsement you obtain for the first time. There is no federal ELDT renewal or refresher.

### What if my ELDT doesn't show up after two business days?
Contact your training provider first; only providers can submit records. If the provider confirms submission, ask your state licensing agency to re-check the TPR.

### Does failing the skills test reset my ELDT?
No. Your training record stays in the registry. You retest under your state's retest rules.

---

# How Much Does It Cost to Get a CDL?

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/how-much-does-it-cost-to-get-a-cdl
Updated: 2026-11-16

**Getting a CDL typically costs about $3,500 to $10,000 at a private CDL school, mostly for training.** You can spend much less by doing ELDT theory online ($119.99 to $129.99 here for Class A or B) and buying behind-the-wheel training separately, or almost nothing upfront with employer-paid or company-sponsored training. Non-training costs (DOT physical, permit, skills test, license) usually add a few hundred dollars depending on your state.

## CDL cost breakdown

| Cost | Typical range | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| ELDT theory | $50 to $150 online | Class A $129.99, Class B $119.99 at ELDT Training |
| Behind-the-wheel training | ~$1,500 to $5,000+ | Hourly or packaged; varies widely |
| Full CDL school (theory + BTW) | ~$3,000 to $10,000 | Often includes test-day truck |
| DOT physical | ~$75 to $150 | National Registry examiner |
| CLP fee | Varies by state | Often includes knowledge tests |
| Skills test fee | Varies by state | Some states use paid third-party testers |
| CDL license fee | Varies by state | Plus endorsement fees |
| Truck for skills test | $0 to several hundred | Usually included with BTW programs |
| TSA threat assessment (H/X) | Under $100 | Paid to TSA's enrollment provider |

State fees vary a lot. Check your state licensing agency's fee schedule; our [state pages](/pages/state) link to each agency.

## Three ways to pay for a CDL

### 1. Private CDL school: highest cost, most convenience
One provider handles theory, BTW, and often the test truck. Expect roughly $3,000 to $10,000 for Class A.

### 2. Online ELDT theory + separate BTW: often the best value
Finish federally required theory online at your own pace, then buy only the BTW training you need from a registered provider. This often cuts total cost and lets you keep working while you study.

### 3. Employer-paid or company-sponsored training: lowest upfront cost
Carriers, school districts, transit agencies, and municipalities may pay for training, sometimes with a work commitment. Read repayment terms carefully. See [paid CDL training](/guides/paid-cdl-training).

## Hidden costs to budget for

- Retest fees if you fail a knowledge or skills test
- Travel to a test site and time off work
- Medical specialist visits if your DOT exam needs extra paperwork
- Renewals: medical certificate (up to every 24 months) and hazmat threat assessment (every 5 years)

## Frequently asked questions

### What's the cheapest way to get a CDL?
Employer-paid training is cheapest upfront. If you're paying yourself, online ELDT theory plus BTW-only training is usually cheaper than an all-inclusive school.

### Is a Class B CDL cheaper than Class A?
Usually. Class B BTW is shorter and Class B theory is a bit cheaper ($119.99 vs $129.99 here). But Class A qualifies you for more jobs and also lets you take the Class B skills test.

### Can I use financial aid for a CDL?
Some community college CDL programs accept federal financial aid, and WIOA workforce funding or GI Bill benefits may cover approved programs.

### How much do CDL endorsements cost?
Expect state knowledge-test and endorsement fees, plus ELDT for H, P, or S ($59.99 to $69.99 online here), and the TSA assessment for hazmat.

# How Old Do You Have to Be to Get a CDL?

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/how-old-to-get-a-cdl
Updated: 2026-11-16

**You must be at least 18 to get a CDL in most states, but drivers under 21 are limited to intrastate driving (within one state).** Federal rules (49 CFR 391.11) require you to be **21 to drive a commercial vehicle in interstate commerce**, and in practice 21 to haul placarded hazmat. ELDT rules apply the same way at any age: if you're getting your first Class A or B CDL, you need ELDT before your skills test.

## CDL age rules at a glance

| Age | What you can do |
|---|---|
| Under 18 | No CDL |
| 18 to 20 | CLP and CDL in most states, **intrastate only** (often shown as a K restriction) |
| 21+ | Interstate driving, most hazmat work, full CDL privileges |

## Why 18-year-olds are limited to intrastate

The federal driver qualification rules require interstate commercial drivers to be at least 21. States can license 18- to 20-year-olds for intrastate commerce, so a young driver can haul freight between cities in the same state but not across state lines. Federal pilot programs for under-21 interstate drivers have been very limited, so plan on intrastate work until you turn 21.

## What jobs can you get with a CDL under 21?

- Local and regional delivery within your state
- Construction, dump truck, and concrete work
- Agricultural hauling
- Municipal and utility work
- Some intrastate company driver jobs at larger carriers

Many large interstate carriers hire at 21 and up, and some require 22 or 23 for insurance reasons.

## Age and endorsements

- **Hazmat (H):** most states and the hazmat transportation rules effectively require you to be 21.
- **Passenger and School Bus:** many states and employers set minimum ages of 21 or older for school bus drivers.
- **Tanker and Doubles/Triples:** follow the general CDL age rules, but employers often require experience.

## Do younger drivers need ELDT?

Yes. ELDT is based on the license you're getting, not your age. An 18-year-old getting a first-time Class A CDL needs [Class A ELDT](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-a) theory and BTW, exactly like a 40-year-old.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I get a CDL at 17?
No. The minimum age for a CLP or CDL is 18 in every state.

### Can I start ELDT before I turn 18?
FMCSA doesn't set an age for theory training, but you can't get a CLP or take the skills test until you meet your state's age requirement. Check with your provider and state.

### Is there a maximum age for a CDL?
No. As long as you meet the medical and other requirements, there's no upper age limit.

### Does the intrastate restriction come off automatically at 21?
It depends on the state. Many require you to visit and request removal of the K restriction once you turn 21 and have a valid medical certificate.

---

# How to Get a CDL Without Going to CDL School

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/how-to-get-a-cdl-without-school
Updated: 2026-11-16

**Yes, you can get a CDL without attending a traditional CDL school, but you can't skip training.** Since February 7, 2022, first-time Class A and B applicants must complete ELDT from providers on the FMCSA Training Provider Registry. The most common "no school" path is: ELDT theory online, then behind-the-wheel training from an employer that's registered as a provider, a BTW-only provider, or a community program. Theory and BTW can come from different registered providers.

## What changed in 2022

Before ELDT, you could study the manual, practice with any CDL holder, and test. Now your state must see ELDT theory **and** BTW records in the Training Provider Registry before your skills test. Practice with a friend or family member can still help, but it doesn't replace registered BTW training.

## Ways to get your CDL without a traditional school

### Online theory + BTW-only provider
Complete theory online (Class A $129.99 here), then buy BTW from a registered provider that sells range and road training separately. This is often the cheapest self-funded route.

### Online theory + employer BTW
Many carriers, construction companies, municipalities, and bus operators are registered BTW providers. Some will hire you with a CLP, train you, and pay for testing. Online theory you've already completed can make you more attractive to these employers.

### Company-sponsored programs
Some carriers run full programs at no upfront cost with a work commitment. See [paid CDL training](/guides/paid-cdl-training).

### Community colleges and workforce programs
Not exactly "no school," but often cheaper and sometimes grant-funded.

## Step-by-step

1. DOT physical and CLP knowledge tests.
2. [Online ELDT theory](/collections/all) for your class.
3. Find a TPR-registered BTW provider (search the [registry](/guides/training-provider-registry)).
4. Hold your CLP 14 days and complete BTW.
5. Take the skills test in a representative vehicle (your BTW provider may supply it).

## What you still can't skip

- Registered BTW training for Class A, B, P, and S
- The 14-day CLP holding period
- State knowledge and skills tests
- The DOT medical exam and Clearinghouse check

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I get a CDL in Texas without school?
Yes, the same federal rules apply in every state: online ELDT theory from a registered provider plus registered BTW training. Texas DPS checks the TPR before the skills test. See [ELDT in Texas](/pages/state/tx).

### Can a family member with a CDL train me?
They can ride along while you practice with your CLP, but unless they're a qualified instructor with a TPR-registered provider, that practice doesn't count as ELDT BTW.

### Can I rent a truck for my skills test?
Some providers and test sites rent trucks. You'll still need registered BTW training before testing.

### Is online CDL training legitimate?
The theory portion, yes, when the provider is on the TPR. There's no legitimate "fully online CDL."

---

# How to Get a CDL: Step-by-Step Guide for 2026

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/how-to-get-a-cdl
Updated: 2026-11-16

**To get a CDL: (1) choose your license class and endorsements, (2) pass a DOT physical, (3) pass your state's CDL knowledge tests to get a commercial learner's permit (CLP), (4) hold the CLP at least 14 days, (5) complete ELDT theory and behind-the-wheel training with FMCSA-registered providers, and (6) pass the CDL skills test.** You must be at least 18 (21 to drive across state lines). With focused effort, many people finish in 4 to 8 weeks.

Minimum age: 18 intrastate / 21 interstate
CLP holding period: 14 days minimum
ELDT required: Yes, for first-time Class A and B
Skills test parts: Inspection, basic control, road
Typical timeline: 4 to 8 weeks

## Step 1: Choose your CDL class and endorsements

- **Class A:** tractor-trailers and other combinations over 26,000 lbs towing more than 10,000 lbs. The most flexible license. See [Class A CDL](/guides/class-a-cdl).
- **Class B:** heavy single vehicles such as dump trucks, box trucks, and buses. See [Class B CDL](/guides/class-b-cdl).
- **Class C:** smaller vehicles carrying 16+ passengers or placarded hazmat. See [ELDT for Class C](/guides/eldt-class-c).

Then decide on [endorsements](/guides/cdl-endorsements): Hazmat (H), Tanker (N), Passenger (P), School Bus (S), Doubles/Triples (T), or X. Not sure? Read [Class A vs Class B](/guides/class-a-vs-class-b-cdl).

## Step 2: Meet the basic requirements

You'll need a valid non-commercial driver's license, proof of identity, U.S. citizenship or lawful presence, state residency, and a Social Security number. You must be able to read and speak English well enough to do the job. Your state will also check your driving record and the FMCSA Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse. Full list: [CDL requirements](/guides/cdl-requirements).

## Step 3: Pass a DOT physical

Get a DOT physical from a medical examiner listed on the FMCSA National Registry. If you pass, you'll receive a medical examiner's certificate, valid for up to 24 months. See [DOT physical and medical card](/guides/dot-physical-medical-card).

## Step 4: Get your commercial learner's permit (CLP)

Study your state's CDL manual and pass the knowledge tests at your state licensing agency:

- **General Knowledge** (everyone)
- **Air Brakes** (if you'll drive air-brake vehicles, which most trucks have)
- **Combination Vehicles** (Class A)
- Endorsement tests you need (P, S, N, H, T)

You must hold your CLP for **at least 14 days** before taking the skills test. A CLP is valid for up to one year depending on your state. See [CDL permit (CLP) guide](/guides/cdl-permit-clp) and [CDL permit test](/guides/cdl-permit-test).

## Step 5: Complete ELDT theory training

If you're getting a Class A or B CDL for the first time (or upgrading B to A), you must complete ELDT theory with a provider on the FMCSA Training Provider Registry and score 80% or higher. Theory can be done online, before or after you get your CLP. Our [Class A](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-a) and [Class B](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-b) courses are self-paced and reported to the TPR when you pass.

## Step 6: Complete behind-the-wheel training

Train in a real truck with a TPR-registered BTW provider (a CDL school, community college, or carrier program), on a range and on public roads. There's no minimum hours; your instructor certifies when you're proficient. See [theory vs behind-the-wheel](/guides/eldt-theory-vs-behind-the-wheel).

## Step 7: Pass the CDL skills test

Your state checks the TPR for your ELDT records, then you take the three-part skills test in a vehicle representative of your license class:

1. **Vehicle inspection** (pre-trip)
2. **Basic vehicle control** (backing maneuvers)
3. **On-road driving test**

Prepare with our [pre-trip inspection checklist](/guides/pre-trip-inspection-checklist) and [CDL skills test guide](/guides/cdl-skills-test).

## Step 8: Get your CDL and start driving

Pass the skills test, pay your state fee, and receive your CDL. Keep your medical certificate current, and remember that adding a first-time H, P, or S endorsement later requires ELDT for that endorsement.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I get a CDL without going to CDL school?
Yes, as long as you complete ELDT theory and BTW with registered providers. Many drivers take theory online and BTW from an employer or a BTW-only provider. See [how to get a CDL without school](/guides/how-to-get-a-cdl-without-school).

### How hard is it to get a CDL?
It takes real study and practice, but most people who prepare pass. The parts that trip people up most are the air brakes knowledge test, the pre-trip inspection, and backing maneuvers.

### How long does it take to get a CDL?
Typically 4 to 8 weeks with focused effort, with a 14-day minimum between getting your CLP and taking the skills test. See [how long it takes to get a CDL](/guides/how-long-does-it-take-to-get-a-cdl).

### How much does it cost to get a CDL?
Anywhere from a few hundred dollars (if an employer covers BTW) to $10,000+ at private schools. See [CDL cost](/guides/how-much-does-it-cost-to-get-a-cdl).

### Can I get a CDL in a different state than I live in?
You generally must get your CDL from your state of domicile. You can train elsewhere, and some states let you take the skills test out of state and have results transferred.

---

# Online ELDT Training: How It Works and How to Know It's Legit

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/online-eldt-training
Updated: 2026-11-16

**Yes. FMCSA allows ELDT theory training to be completed 100% online**, as long as the provider is listed on the FMCSA Training Provider Registry and the content is prepared by qualified theory instructors. Online theory is accepted in every state. You still need in-person behind-the-wheel training for Class A, Class B, Passenger (P), and School Bus (S). The Hazmat (H) endorsement is theory only, so it can be completed entirely online.

## How online ELDT theory training works

1. **Enroll** in the course that matches your license or endorsement (Class A, Class B, B-to-A upgrade, H, P, or S).
2. **Get your login** by email and start right away. There is no class schedule.
3. **Work through the lessons** at your own pace on a phone, tablet, or computer. Good courses save your progress automatically and include audio narration.
4. **Take the quizzes and final assessment.** You need an overall score of **80% or higher**.
5. **The provider reports your completion** to the Training Provider Registry, within the federal deadline of midnight on the second business day.
6. **Your state sees it.** Your licensing agency checks the registry before your skills test (or H knowledge test).

## What you can and can't do online

| Training | Online? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Class A theory | Yes | Then BTW range + public road |
| Class B theory | Yes | Then BTW range + public road |
| Class B to A upgrade theory | Yes | Then Class A BTW |
| Hazmat (H) theory | Yes | No BTW, fully online |
| Passenger (P) theory | Yes | Then P BTW |
| School Bus (S) theory | Yes | Then S BTW |
| Behind-the-wheel (any) | No | In a real vehicle with a qualified instructor; simulators can't replace it |

## Is online ELDT legit?

Online theory is explicitly allowed by FMCSA. The question to ask is whether the **provider** is legitimate. A course only counts if the provider is listed on the TPR at the time you train. Since December 2025, FMCSA has removed thousands of non-compliant or inactive providers from the registry, and training conducted after a provider's removal date is invalid.

Before you pay, check that the provider:

- Appears on the [FMCSA Training Provider Registry](/guides/training-provider-registry) search, with **theory** listed for your training type
- Clearly states which training types it offers (Class A, Class B, P, S, H)
- Explains how and when it reports completions to the TPR
- Requires a final assessment with an 80% passing score (no "instant certificate" shortcuts)
- Lists real contact information and a refund policy

## Benefits of online ELDT theory

- **Lower cost.** Online theory usually costs a fraction of classroom programs. See [ELDT cost](/guides/eldt-cost).
- **Flexible schedule.** Study around your current job, at night, or on weekends.
- **Faster start.** Begin the same day you enroll; no waiting for a class to fill.
- **Self-paced.** Spend more time on topics that are new to you and move faster through what you already know.
- **Audio playback.** Listen to lessons, which helps if you learn better by hearing.

## Things to know before you buy

- **Language:** Many online courses, including ours, are English only. Federal rules also require CDL drivers to read and speak English well enough to do the job. See our guide to [English language proficiency for CDL drivers](/guides/cdl-english-language-proficiency).
- **Your name and license number matter.** The record sent to the TPR must match your driver's license or CLP, so enter your information exactly.
- **BTW is separate.** Line up a registered BTW provider (CDL school, community college, or carrier training program) for Class A, B, P, and S.
- **Completion windows:** Our courses give you 3 months to finish and 1 year of access to review materials.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is online ELDT accepted in my state?
Yes. ELDT is a federal requirement and every state checks the same national registry, so online theory from a TPR-registered provider is accepted in all 50 states and DC. Find your state on our [ELDT by state](/pages/state) page.

### How long does online ELDT take?
It depends on the course and your pace. Our Class A course is about 15 hours, Class B about 13 hours, and the hazmat course about 5 hours. There is no federal minimum.

### Can I do ELDT online for free?
Legitimate ELDT theory from a registered provider is rarely free unless an employer, workforce program, or school pays for it. See [free ELDT training options](/guides/free-eldt-training).

### Can I get my whole CDL online?
No. Theory can be online, but you must complete behind-the-wheel training in person (for Class A and B) and pass the in-person CDL skills test at a state-approved test site.

### Is online ELDT available in Spanish?
Some providers offer Spanish courses. Our courses are English only, with audio playback.
