# Paid CDL Training: How Company-Sponsored Programs Work

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/paid-cdl-training
Updated: 2026-11-16

**Paid (company-sponsored) CDL training means an employer covers your CDL training, including ELDT theory and behind-the-wheel, usually in exchange for agreeing to drive for them for a set period, often around a year.** Some programs pay you during training. If you leave early, you may have to repay part or all of the training cost. These programs must still use providers on the FMCSA Training Provider Registry, so your ELDT records are valid anywhere.

## How company-sponsored training usually works

1. **Apply and get conditionally hired** (background, driving record, drug test, DOT physical).
2. **Get your CLP**, often with the company's help.
3. **Complete ELDT theory and BTW** through the company's registered school or a partner school.
4. **Pass the skills test**, often in the company's truck.
5. **Drive with a trainer** for a period of supervised over-the-road experience.
6. **Fulfill the work commitment** to have the training cost forgiven.

## Types of paid CDL training

| Type | How it's paid | Typical catch |
|---|---|---|
| Company-sponsored school | Carrier pays tuition | Work commitment; repayment if you leave |
| Tuition reimbursement | You pay, carrier reimburses over time | Must stay employed to get full reimbursement |
| Paid training (wages) | Carrier pays you while training | Often lower pay during training phase |
| Public employer programs | District, transit, or city pays | Usually local jobs, sometimes a commitment |

## Questions to ask before you sign

- How long is the work commitment, and how is the repayment amount calculated if I leave early?
- Is the repayment prorated?
- Are you a TPR-registered provider, or which registered school will train me?
- Am I paid during training? How much, and for which phases?
- What kind of runs will I do after training (OTR, regional, local), and how much home time?
- What happens if I fail a test?

## An alternative: do theory yourself

Completing [ELDT theory online](/collections/all) on your own can make you a stronger applicant, shorten company training, and give you more options, including employers that only provide BTW. Online theory is $119.99 to $129.99 here for Class B or A.

## Frequently asked questions

### Which trucking companies pay for CDL training?
Many large truckload and LTL carriers, as well as some private fleets, run company-sponsored or tuition-reimbursement programs. Offerings change often, so check carriers' current recruiting pages and compare contracts.

### Is paid CDL training really free?
The upfront cost may be zero, but you usually owe a work commitment, and leaving early can mean repaying training costs.

### Is my ELDT from a company program valid with other employers?
Yes. ELDT records in the Training Provider Registry belong to your driver record, not the employer. Your CDL is yours.

### Can I get paid CDL training with housing?
Some programs provide lodging during training, especially when the school is far from home. Ask what's included.

---

# Passenger Endorsement (P): How to Get It

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/passenger-endorsement
Updated: 2026-11-16

**A Passenger (P) endorsement is required to drive a commercial vehicle designed to transport 16 or more passengers, including the driver.** To get it for the first time, you complete P endorsement ELDT (theory plus behind-the-wheel training) with FMCSA-registered providers, pass the passenger knowledge test, and pass a skills test in a passenger vehicle of the right class. School bus drivers need the P endorsement plus the S endorsement.

## Who needs a passenger endorsement?

- City, transit, and paratransit bus drivers
- Motorcoach, charter, and tour bus drivers
- Airport, hotel, and casino shuttle drivers (vehicles designed for 16+)
- School bus drivers (with the S endorsement)
- Church, camp, and nonprofit drivers of large buses

The vehicle's **design capacity** matters, not how many people are actually on board.

## How to get a P endorsement

1. **Hold a CDL or CLP** of the right class (B for most full-size buses, C for smaller ones, A in some cases).
2. **Pass the passenger knowledge test** (it can be added to your CLP, but you can't carry passengers until fully endorsed).
3. **Complete P endorsement ELDT theory.** Our [Passenger (P) course](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-passenger-p-endorsement) is 18 lessons, about 6 hours, for $59.99.
4. **Complete P endorsement BTW** with a registered provider in a passenger vehicle.
5. **Pass the skills test** in a passenger vehicle of the class you're licensed for.

## What P endorsement ELDT covers

Vehicle orientation, pre-trip/en route/post-trip inspection, fueling and idling, post-crash and emergency procedures, passenger management and baggage, hours of service, seat belt rules, railroad crossings, navigating highways and tunnels, security awareness, and roadside inspections.

## P endorsement on Class A, B, or C

| CDL class | Typical vehicles |
|---|---|
| Class B + P | Full-size transit buses, motorcoaches, many school buses |
| Class C + P | Smaller buses and passenger vans designed for 16+ under 26,001 lbs |
| Class A + P | Articulated buses or bus-plus-trailer combinations, plus everything below |

Testing in a smaller class of vehicle may add an M or N passenger restriction. See [CDL restrictions](/guides/cdl-restrictions).

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need ELDT for a passenger endorsement?
Yes, if you're getting P for the first time and didn't hold it before February 7, 2022. You need both theory and behind-the-wheel training.

### Do I need a CDL to drive a 15-passenger van?
Generally no, if it's designed for 15 or fewer occupants including the driver. Vehicles designed for 16 or more require a CDL with P.

### How many questions are on the passenger endorsement test?
Typically around 20, with an 80% passing score. Format varies by state.

### Can I get the P endorsement on my permit?
Yes, P can appear on a CLP, but CLP holders with P may not carry passengers other than trainers, examiners, and other trainees.

---

# CDL Pre-Trip Inspection Checklist for Class A and Class B

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/pre-trip-inspection-checklist
Updated: 2026-11-16

**A CDL pre-trip inspection follows a set order: engine compartment, cab check and engine start, in-cab air brake test, external lights, a walk-around of steering, suspension, brakes, wheels and tires on each axle, then coupling and trailer (Class A).** On the skills test you must point to each item, name it, and say what you're checking for (for example, "mounted securely, not cracked, bent, or broken"). Federal rules also require drivers to be satisfied the vehicle is in safe operating condition before every trip.

For most components, say what it is and that it is "properly mounted and secure, not cracked, bent, broken, or leaking." For hoses and lines add "not cut, chafed, or worn." For fluids, check level and leaks.

## 1. Engine compartment

- Fluid levels and leaks: oil, coolant, power steering
- Water pump, alternator, and air compressor, with belts (tension, wear)
- Hoses (cracks, wear, leaks)
- Steering box, steering linkage
- Wiring (secure, insulation intact)

## 2. Cab check and engine start

- Clutch and gearshift (if manual), parking brake set
- Gauges after start: oil pressure rising, air pressure building, coolant temperature, voltmeter
- Warning lights and buzzers clear
- Mirrors and windshield clean, not cracked; wipers and washers work
- Horns (air and electric), heater/defroster
- Lights: headlights, high beams, four-way flashers, turn signals
- Emergency equipment: fire extinguisher (charged), three reflective triangles, spare fuses if required
- Seat belt secure and working

## 3. In-cab air brake test (air-brake vehicles)

| Check | Standard to know |
|---|---|
| Air pressure build-up | Typically 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds (dual systems, at operating RPM) |
| Governor cut-out | Commonly about 120 to 140 psi |
| Static leak (brakes released) | No more than 2 psi/min single vehicle, 3 psi/min combination |
| Applied leak (brakes held) | No more than 3 psi/min single, 4 psi/min combination after initial drop |
| Low air warning | Activates at or before 60 psi |
| Spring brakes / parking valve | Pop out between about 20 and 45 psi |
| Parking brake check | Vehicle shouldn't move in low gear with parking brake set |
| Service brake check | Vehicle stops straight at about 5 mph |

Values above follow the national model CDL manual; use your state manual's numbers on the test.

## 4. External inspection: lights and front

Headlights, turn signals, clearance and marker lights, reflectors; windshield; front bumper; steering axle tires and wheels.

## 5. Steering and suspension (each axle)

Steering components (no looseness), springs (no broken leaves), spring mounts, shock absorbers, air bags (if equipped), torque arms.

## 6. Brakes (each axle)

Slack adjusters and push rods (adjustment, not more than about 1 inch of travel when pulled by hand on manual adjusters), brake chambers, brake hoses and lines, drums or rotors, linings (not worn dangerously thin, no oil contamination).

## 7. Wheels and tires (each axle)

| Item | What to check |
|---|---|
| Tread depth | At least 4/32 inch on steering axle tires, 2/32 inch on other tires |
| Tire condition | No cuts, bulges, exposed cords, mismatched sizes, or dual tires touching |
| Inflation | Properly inflated (check with a gauge) |
| Rims | Not cracked, bent, or with illegal welds |
| Lug nuts | All present and tight, no rust trails |
| Hub oil seal | Not leaking; oil level OK if visible |
| Valve stems | Present, not damaged |

## 8. Coupling system (Class A)

- Air and electrical lines (glad hands sealed, no leaks, not tangled or dragging)
- Fifth wheel mounting and platform (secure, no cracks), lubrication
- Locking jaws closed around the kingpin shank, release arm in locked position
- Kingpin and apron (not bent or damaged), no gap between apron and fifth wheel
- Sliding fifth wheel locked (if equipped)

## 9. Trailer

Landing gear (raised, handle secured), frame and crossmembers, doors and hinges, tandem release (locked), lights and reflectors, trailer brakes, wheels and tires, suspension.

## 10. Bus additions (P and S)

Passenger entry door and steps, emergency exits and alarms, seats secure, first-aid kit; for school buses, stop arm, crossing arm, alternating red and amber lights, and student mirrors.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there a printable pre-trip inspection checklist?
You can print this page from your browser. Your state's CDL manual also includes a pre-trip section, and some states publish their own skills test inspection forms.

### How long does the pre-trip take on the skills test?
Usually 30 to 60 minutes depending on the vehicle and state. Practice until you can do it smoothly in order.

### Do I have to memorize the whole truck?
You need to name each component the examiner selects and explain what you're checking. Most states test a subset, but you won't know which parts in advance.

### Does ELDT cover pre-trip inspection?
Yes. Pre- and post-trip inspections are part of the ELDT theory curriculum, and you'll practice them during behind-the-wheel training.

---

# School Bus Endorsement (S): How to Get It

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/school-bus-endorsement
Updated: 2026-11-16

**To drive a school bus you need a CDL (usually Class B, sometimes C) with both the Passenger (P) and School Bus (S) endorsements.** First-time applicants must complete ELDT for each endorsement (theory and behind-the-wheel) with FMCSA-registered providers, plus Class B ELDT if it's your first Class B CDL. Then you pass the school bus and passenger knowledge tests and a skills test in a school bus. Most states also require background checks and their own school bus driver training.

## The full list of what a new school bus driver needs

| Requirement | Details |
|---|---|
| CDL class | Class B for most full-size school buses; Class C for smaller buses |
| Class B ELDT | If it's your first Class B CDL ([course](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-b)) |
| P endorsement ELDT | Theory + BTW ([course](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-passenger-p-endorsement)) |
| S endorsement ELDT | Theory + BTW ([course](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-school-bus-s-endorsement)) |
| Knowledge tests | General Knowledge, Air Brakes (if equipped), Passenger, School Bus |
| Skills test | In a school bus of the class you're licensed for |
| State requirements | Commonly fingerprint background check, driving record review, pre-service training, annual refresher |

## What S endorsement ELDT covers

The school bus curriculum (Appendix D to Part 380) focuses on danger zones and mirror use, loading and unloading, student management, emergency exit and evacuation, railroad-highway grade crossings, antilock braking systems, and special safety considerations. Our S course is 11 lessons, about 5 hours, for $59.99.

## Step-by-step path to becoming a school bus driver

1. Apply with a school district or contractor (many pay for training and testing).
2. DOT physical and CLP with P and S knowledge tests (S and P can appear on a CLP; no passengers allowed while on a CLP).
3. Complete Class B, P, and S ELDT theory online.
4. Complete BTW in a school bus with a registered provider (often the district itself).
5. Pass the skills test in a school bus.
6. Complete your state's school bus certification requirements.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do school bus drivers need both P and S?
Yes. Federal rules require the P endorsement for vehicles designed for 16+ occupants, and the S endorsement specifically for school buses.

### Does my school district pay for training?
Many districts and contractors pay for CDL training, ELDT, and testing, and some pay you while you train. Ask during hiring.

### Can I drive a school bus with a Class C CDL?
For smaller school buses under 26,001 lbs GVWR, yes, with P and S endorsements. Full-size buses require Class B.

### Is the school bus endorsement test hard?
The knowledge test is typically about 20 questions. The skills test includes school-bus-specific inspection items and procedures like loading and unloading and railroad crossings, so practice them during BTW.

---

# Tanker Endorsement (N): Requirements, Test, and How to Get It

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/tanker-endorsement
Updated: 2026-11-16

**A tanker (N) endorsement is required to drive a CMV that carries liquid or gaseous materials in tanks with an individual rated capacity over 119 gallons and an aggregate capacity of 1,000 gallons or more** (49 CFR 383.5). To get it, you pass your state's tank vehicle knowledge test; there's no skills test and no federal ELDT requirement. If you'll haul hazmat in a tank, you need the X endorsement (or H plus N) instead.

## What counts as a tank vehicle?

A tank vehicle is any CMV designed to transport liquid or gaseous materials in tanks that are permanently or temporarily attached to the vehicle or chassis, with:

- Any single tank rated **over 119 gallons**, and
- A combined (aggregate) rated capacity of **1,000 gallons or more**

Examples: fuel tankers, milk and food-grade tankers, water trucks, and flatbeds carrying large IBC totes that meet the capacity thresholds. Empty tanks still count; the endorsement depends on the vehicle's design capacity.

## How to get a tanker endorsement

1. Hold a CDL or CLP (N can be placed on a CLP, but CLP holders may only drive empty tanks).
2. Study the tank vehicle section of your state's CDL manual, or take a [tanker training course](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-tanker-n-endorsement).
3. Pass the tank vehicle knowledge test (typically about 20 questions with an 80% passing score).
4. Pay your state's endorsement fee.

## Does the tanker endorsement require ELDT?

No. The federal ELDT rule covers Class A, Class B, and the H, P, and S endorsements. Tank vehicle training is still valuable, and many carriers require documented tanker training before you haul.

## What's on the tanker test

- **Liquid surge** and how it affects stopping and handling
- **Baffles and bulkheads** vs **smooth-bore tanks**
- **High center of gravity** and rollover risk on curves and ramps
- **Outage** (allowing room for liquid expansion)
- Inspection of valves, manhole covers, vents, and emergency shutoffs
- Braking and following distance with partial loads

## Tanker (N) vs X endorsement

| | N | X |
|---|---|---|
| Covers | Non-hazmat liquids/gases in tanks | Hazmat in tanks (and non-hazmat) |
| Tests | Tanker knowledge | Tanker + hazmat knowledge |
| TSA check | No | Yes |
| ELDT | No | Hazmat theory (if no H yet) |
| Our course | [$49.99](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-tanker-n-endorsement) | [$129.99](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-hazmat-and-tank-vehicle-endorsement) |

## Frequently asked questions

### When do you need a tanker endorsement?
Whenever the vehicle's tanks meet the 119-gallon individual and 1,000-gallon aggregate thresholds, loaded or empty.

### How many questions are on the tanker endorsement test?
Typically around 20, with 80% needed to pass, though formats vary by state.

### Is the tanker endorsement hard?
It's one of the easier endorsements. Focus on liquid surge, baffles, and rollover prevention.

### Do I need a tanker endorsement to haul IBC totes?
If the totes are each over 119 gallons and total 1,000 gallons or more, and are loaded on the vehicle, the vehicle can meet the tank vehicle definition. Check with your carrier.

---

# FMCSA Training Provider Registry (TPR): What It Is and How to Use It

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/training-provider-registry
Updated: 2026-11-16

**The FMCSA Training Provider Registry (TPR) at tpr.fmcsa.dot.gov is the official federal list of organizations allowed to deliver Entry-Level Driver Training, and the system that stores each driver's ELDT completion records.** Only training from a provider listed on the TPR counts. Providers must report your completion by midnight of the second business day, and your state licensing agency checks the TPR before your CDL skills test or H knowledge test. Always search the registry before you pay for training.

## What the TPR does

- **Lists registered providers.** Schools, carriers, community colleges, unions, school districts, and online providers self-certify that they meet 49 CFR Part 380 requirements and receive a TPR identification number.
- **Stores driver training records.** Providers submit each driver's completed theory and BTW training.
- **Feeds state licensing agencies.** States query the TPR before administering the relevant test.
- **Lets FMCSA remove providers.** FMCSA can propose removal of providers that don't meet the requirements and remove them from the registry.

## How to check a provider on the TPR

1. Go to **tpr.fmcsa.dot.gov** and choose the option to search for a training provider.
2. Search by provider name, city, state, or ZIP code.
3. Open the listing and confirm the **training types** offered (Class A, Class B, P, S, H) and whether it offers **theory**, **BTW range**, and/or **BTW public road**.
4. For in-person training, confirm the **location** where you'll train is listed.
5. Check that the provider is **active** (not removed or under a notice of proposed removal).

Training delivered after a provider's removal date is invalid under federal rules. If a provider receives a notice of proposed removal, it must tell enrolled students.

## TPR removals since 2025: what drivers should know

FMCSA has significantly stepped up enforcement of the registry. In December 2025, FMCSA announced the removal of more than 3,000 providers and sent notices of proposed removal to thousands more. In 2026 FMCSA continued removing providers, including emergency removals tied to compliance problems. Many removed listings were inactive, but the lesson for drivers is the same:

- **Verify before you enroll**, not after.
- **Keep your receipts and certificate** of completion.
- **Complete training promptly** once you start.
- If your provider is removed while you're mid-training, **contact your state licensing agency** before you test.

## How the TPR handles your record

1. You complete theory (80%+) or BTW.
2. The provider submits your name, license number and state, training type, and completion date with its TPR ID.
3. The record becomes available to state licensing agencies.
4. Before your test, the state verifies the record. No record, no test.

Drivers can't submit or edit records; only the provider that trained you can correct a record it submitted. See [ELDT certificate](/guides/eldt-certificate) for troubleshooting.

## Is ELDT Training on the registry?

Yes. ELDTtraining.us is a registered training provider on the FMCSA Training Provider Registry for ELDT theory, and we report each completion to the TPR as soon as you pass the final assessment. You can verify any provider, including us, by searching the registry directly.

## Choosing between registered providers

Being on the TPR is the minimum bar. To compare providers, look at price, course length and format, audio and mobile support, how fast they report, support hours, and refund policy. See [how to choose the best online ELDT provider](/guides/best-online-eldt-training).

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the TPR in trucking?
TPR stands for Training Provider Registry, FMCSA's database of approved Entry-Level Driver Training providers and the driver training records those providers submit.

### Are "FMCSA approved" and "TPR registered" the same thing?
FMCSA does not individually approve or endorse schools. Providers self-certify and are listed on the TPR, and FMCSA can audit and remove them. "Listed on the TPR" is the accurate term.

### How do I know if my ELDT was submitted to the TPR?
Ask your provider for the submission date. Providers must submit by midnight of the second business day after completion. Your state will confirm when you schedule or arrive for your test.

### Can an employer use the TPR?
Employers can search the registry to verify providers. Carriers that train their own drivers can register as providers themselves. See [ELDT for employers](/guides/eldt-for-employers).

### What happens to my record if my school closes?
Records already submitted remain in the registry. If your school closed before submitting, contact your state licensing agency.

---

# What Is ELDT? Entry-Level Driver Training Explained

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/what-is-eldt
Updated: 2026-11-16

**ELDT (Entry-Level Driver Training) is a Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) rule that sets the minimum training new commercial drivers must complete before they can take certain CDL tests.** It applies to anyone getting a Class A or Class B CDL for the first time, upgrading from Class B to Class A, or getting a Hazmat (H), Passenger (P), or School Bus (S) endorsement for the first time. Training must come from a provider listed on the FMCSA Training Provider Registry (TPR), and it has two parts: theory (which can be done online) and behind-the-wheel training.

Stands for: Entry-Level Driver Training
Regulation: 49 CFR Part 380, Subparts F and G
In effect since: February 7, 2022
Theory passing score: 80%
Minimum hours: None (proficiency-based)

## What does ELDT stand for?

ELDT stands for **Entry-Level Driver Training**. You will see it written as "ELDT," "the ELDT rule," or "the ELDT mandate." It refers to the training requirements in 49 CFR Part 380, Subpart F, and the registry of approved trainers in Subpart G.

Before ELDT, there was no national training standard for new CDL drivers. Someone could study the state CDL manual, pass the knowledge test, practice with a friend, and take the skills test. FMCSA created ELDT to make sure every new driver receives the same core knowledge and supervised driving practice from a qualified trainer first.

## Who needs ELDT?

You must complete ELDT before testing if you are:

- Getting a **Class A CDL** for the first time
- Getting a **Class B CDL** for the first time
- **Upgrading** an existing Class B CDL to a Class A CDL
- Getting a **Passenger (P)** endorsement for the first time
- Getting a **School Bus (S)** endorsement for the first time
- Getting a **Hazardous Materials (H)** endorsement for the first time

ELDT is not retroactive. If you held the CDL or endorsement before February 7, 2022, you do not need ELDT for it. ELDT also does not apply to the Tanker (N) or Doubles/Triples (T) endorsements. See our full guide to [ELDT requirements](/guides/eldt-requirements) and [ELDT exemptions](/guides/eldt-exemptions) for the details.

## The two parts of ELDT: theory and behind-the-wheel

**Theory training** is the knowledge portion. It covers federal regulations, vehicle systems, safe operating practices, hours of service, cargo, trip planning, drugs and alcohol, and more. Theory can be delivered online. You must score at least **80%** on the theory assessment.

**Behind-the-wheel (BTW) training** happens in a real commercial vehicle with a qualified instructor. For Class A and Class B it includes both range training (backing, docking, coupling) and public-road training. For P and S endorsements it includes range and/or public-road training specific to buses. The Hazmat (H) endorsement has no BTW requirement.

There is no minimum number of hours for either part. Theory is complete when you pass the assessment; BTW is complete when your instructor determines you are proficient in every required skill. Learn more in [ELDT theory vs behind-the-wheel training](/guides/eldt-theory-vs-behind-the-wheel).

## How ELDT works, step by step

1. **Choose a registered provider.** Every provider must be listed on the [FMCSA Training Provider Registry](/guides/training-provider-registry). You can take theory and BTW from different providers.
2. **Complete theory training.** Online theory lets you study on your schedule. You can start before or after you get your [commercial learner's permit](/guides/cdl-permit-clp).
3. **Complete BTW training** (Class A, B, P, and S only) with a registered BTW provider such as a CDL school or a carrier's training program.
4. **Your provider reports your completion to the TPR** by midnight of the second business day after you finish.
5. **Take your test.** Your state driver licensing agency checks the TPR before it lets you take the CDL skills test (or the H knowledge test).

## Why FMCSA created the ELDT rule

Congress directed FMCSA to set entry-level training standards in the 2012 MAP-21 highway law. FMCSA published the final ELDT rule in December 2016 after a negotiated rulemaking with trucking, bus, safety, and training groups, and set the compliance date as February 7, 2022. The goal is safer roads: drivers who have learned the same core curriculum and shown proficiency to a qualified instructor before they test.

## How much does ELDT cost?

Online theory courses typically cost far less than a full CDL school. At ELDT Training, Class A theory is $129.99, Class B is $119.99, and endorsements start at $49.99. BTW training is usually the larger cost because it requires a truck, a range, and an instructor. See our [ELDT cost guide](/guides/eldt-cost) for a full breakdown.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the meaning of ELDT for CDL?
For CDL applicants, ELDT means the Entry-Level Driver Training you must complete with an FMCSA-registered provider before your state lets you take the Class A or B skills test, the P or S skills test, or the H knowledge test.

### Is ELDT the same as CDL school?
Not exactly. ELDT is the federal minimum training standard. A CDL school is one type of provider that may deliver both parts. You can also complete theory online with one provider and BTW with another, as long as both are on the Training Provider Registry.

### Do I need ELDT if I already have a CDL?
Only if you are upgrading from Class B to Class A or adding a first-time H, P, or S endorsement. Drivers who held their CDL before February 7, 2022 do not need ELDT for that same license class.

### Can ELDT be done online?
The theory portion can be completed entirely online. Behind-the-wheel training cannot; it must be done in a vehicle with a qualified instructor. FMCSA does not allow simulators to replace BTW training.

### What happens if I don't complete ELDT?
Your state licensing agency will not let you take the skills test for Class A, Class B, P, or S, or the knowledge test for H, until a registered provider has reported your training to the TPR.

### Does ELDT expire?
FMCSA's Training Provider Registry FAQs do not set an expiration date for ELDT certification. What does expire is your commercial learner's permit, so plan your training and testing within your CLP's validity. See [how long ELDT training takes](/guides/how-long-is-eldt-training).

---

# What Is the X Endorsement on a CDL?

URL: https://eldttraining.us/guides/x-endorsement
Updated: 2026-11-16

**The X endorsement is a combined Hazardous Materials (H) and Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement.** It lets you haul placarded hazardous materials in tank vehicles, such as gasoline, diesel, and liquid chemicals. To get it, you pass both the hazmat and tanker knowledge tests and the TSA security threat assessment. If you don't already have an H endorsement, you must complete hazmat ELDT theory before the hazmat test.

## What the X endorsement lets you do

- Haul placarded hazmat in tank vehicles (fuel, liquid chemicals, compressed gases)
- Haul non-hazmat liquids in tanks (the N privileges)
- Haul placarded hazmat in non-tank vehicles (the H privileges)

States print X instead of separate H and N codes when you qualify for both.

## Requirements for the X endorsement

| Requirement | Details |
|---|---|
| CDL | Class A, B, or C |
| Hazmat ELDT | Required if you don't already hold H |
| Hazmat knowledge test | Yes |
| Tanker knowledge test | Yes |
| TSA security threat assessment | Yes (fingerprints, fee, background check) |
| Age | In practice, 21+ |

## How to get the X endorsement

1. **Complete hazmat ELDT** (or our X course, which includes hazmat theory plus tank vehicle content).
2. **Start your TSA threat assessment** online and schedule fingerprints.
3. **Pass the hazmat and tanker knowledge tests** at your state licensing agency.
4. **Receive your X endorsement** once TSA approval reaches your state.

Our [X endorsement course](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-hazmat-and-tank-vehicle-endorsement) combines the hazmat ELDT curriculum with tank vehicle operation and inspection in 14 lessons across 5 modules, for $129.99.

## X vs separate H and N courses

| Option | Price at ELDT Training | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| X course | $129.99 | Drivers who want hazmat + tanker in one enrollment |
| H course + N course | $69.99 + $49.99 | Drivers who want them as separate courses |

Either path meets the hazmat ELDT requirement.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is the X endorsement the same as hazmat?
No. X includes hazmat plus tanker. A driver with only H can haul placarded hazmat in non-tank vehicles but not in tank vehicles.

### Does the X endorsement require ELDT?
The hazmat part does, if you're getting hazmat for the first time. The federal ELDT rule doesn't cover the tanker part.

### How much does an X endorsement cost?
Our X course is $129.99. Add the TSA fee (under $100) and your state's test and endorsement fees.

### Is the X endorsement worth it?
For fuel and chemical hauling, yes; it's required. These jobs often pay more than general freight.

# ELDT FAQ: Training Entry-Level Drivers Must Complete

URL: https://eldttraining.us/pages/faq-training-entry-level-driver-must-complete

To be eligible to take the Class A or Class B CDL skills test, the S or P skills test, or the H knowledge test, commercial driver's license (CDL) applicants must complete applicable entry-level driver training from a [registered training provider](/guides/training-provider-registry). The type of training required depends on the license or endorsement you are applying for:

## Frequently asked questions

### What is ELDT?
ELDT (Entry-Level Driver Training) is a set of federal training requirements established by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) in 49 CFR Part 380 for individuals seeking a commercial driver's license or certain CDL endorsements for the first time. Read the full guide: [What is ELDT?](/guides/what-is-eldt)

### Who needs to complete ELDT?
Anyone getting a Class A or Class B CDL for the first time, upgrading from Class B to Class A, or getting a Passenger (P), School Bus (S), or Hazardous Materials (H) endorsement for the first time.

### When did the ELDT requirements take effect?
February 7, 2022. They are not retroactive to individuals who already held the applicable CDL or endorsement before that date.

### Can I complete ELDT training online?
Yes, the theory portion, as long as the provider is on the FMCSA Training Provider Registry. Behind-the-wheel training for Class A, Class B, P, and S must be completed in a vehicle with a qualified instructor.

### What score do I need on the ELDT theory test?
At least 80% overall on the theory assessment.

### How many hours is ELDT?
There's no federal minimum. Our courses run about 15 hours (Class A), 13 (Class B), 12 (B-to-A), 6 (Passenger), and 5 (Hazmat, School Bus, X). See [how long ELDT takes](/guides/how-long-is-eldt-training).

### Do I need my CDL permit before starting ELDT theory?
No. FMCSA doesn't require a CLP before theory training. You need a CLP for behind-the-wheel training on public roads and must hold it 14 days before the skills test.

### Do I need behind-the-wheel training for the hazmat endorsement?
No. The H endorsement requires theory only.

### Can I use different providers for theory and behind-the-wheel?
Yes. Both must be listed on the Training Provider Registry, and each reports its own portion.

### How quickly is my training reported?
Providers must report by midnight of the second business day after completion. We submit as soon as you pass.

### How does my state know I completed ELDT?
Your state driver licensing agency checks the FMCSA Training Provider Registry before the skills test (or the H knowledge test). You don't need to bring a paper certificate, though you can download one from us.

### Does ELDT expire?
FMCSA's Training Provider Registry FAQs don't set an expiration date for ELDT certification. Your commercial learner's permit does expire, so plan to test while it's valid.

### Do I need ELDT for a Tanker (N) or Doubles/Triples (T) endorsement?
No. Federal ELDT covers Class A, Class B, H, P, and S only. Our [Tanker (N) course](/products/cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-tanker-n-endorsement) is optional training to help you pass the N knowledge test.

### Do I need ELDT to upgrade from Class B to Class A?
Yes. A B-to-A upgrade is specifically covered by the ELDT rule. See our [Class B to A upgrade course](/products/entry-level-driver-training-eldt-class-b-to-a-upgrade).

### I already have my learner's permit. Is this course another permit test?
No. If you have your CLP, you've passed your state's written permit tests. ELDT is the federally required training that must be completed and submitted to the Training Provider Registry before your CDL skills test. The course quizzes and final exam are for training completion only and are separate from the DMV tests.

### Is ELDT required in every state?
Yes. It's a federal requirement. Online theory from a registered provider is accepted nationwide. See [ELDT by state](/pages/state).

### Are veterans exempt from ELDT?
Military drivers who qualify for the skills-test waiver under 49 CFR 383.77 aren't subject to ELDT for that license class. See [ELDT exemptions](/guides/eldt-exemptions).

### How much does ELDT cost?
Our online theory courses range from $49.99 to $129.99. Class A is $129.99. See [ELDT cost](/guides/eldt-cost).

### Is the course in Spanish?
No. Our courses are English only, with audio playback that reads each lesson aloud.

### Can my employer pay for my course?
Yes. Employers can purchase courses for drivers. Call (866) 429-6742.

### What's your refund policy?
You can cancel for a full refund within 30 days of purchase, unless 65% or more of the course has been completed or a certificate has been issued. See the full [refund policy](/policies/refund-policy).
